news.Title: Bond Sales Hit €2 Trillion Europe Record as AI Surge Takes Hold
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- Bond sales in Europe have topped €2 trillion ($2.2 trillion) for the first time, as unrelenting government borrowing collides with the vast funding needs of the artificial intelligence boom.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Modi Tries to End Trump Photo-Op in Awkward Viral Moment

Costco Shoppers Are Panic-Buying Due to Outages, Analysts Say

Iran Hit Key Infrastructure, Isn't Behind Tech Outages, US Says

Anthropic IPO Allocates Nothing to Most Institutional Orders

Anthropic Raises $107.3 Billion to Top SpaceX's Record Debut

Tech companies are the biggest driver of the annual record, with US hyperscalers including Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. raising vast sums to finance the data centers and infrastructure needed for AI. With the tech race still gaining speed, borrowing is set to keep European bankers busy.

"Most of the growth in non-financial borrowing is driven by US firms seeking to tap funding from numerous bond markets," HSBC Holdings Plc strategists led by Song Jin Lee wrote this week in their outlook for 2027.

The surge materialized even as higher global interest rates pushed up financing costs, with euro high-grade corporate yields rising to levels last seen in 2023. Investor appetite for corporate debt has remained relatively strong, however, keeping the additional premium companies pay to borrow contained.

The €2 trillion milestone for the publicly syndicated debt market was reached on Thursday, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The record covers syndicated sales in euros, pounds and dollars issued under Regulation S, which allows securities to be sold outside the US without being registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Corporate borrowing is up about €49 billion from 2025, with roughly €37.5 billion of that increase coming from hyperscalers. Alphabet Inc., Amazon.com Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc. each rank among the top four non-financial bond issuers in European currencies this year.

Syndicated sales by governments, multinational institutions and government-backed organizations — which account for roughly 40% of the market — are at record levels but tracking close to last year's figures.

The borrowing binge has downsides. The constant stream of mega-deals by hyperscalers has made investors demand large premiums to invest in new issues. Secondary market trading levels of hyperscalers' euro bonds are in line with bonds rated several steps below their actual scores.

Syndicated sales form part of a larger trend in Europe. Governments, which also borrow via auctions, are using debt to fund spending on defense and infrastructure. Elevated issuance coincides with an increase in yields driven by higher energy costs.

Story Continues

France is contending with growing political and fiscal risks ahead of next year's presidential election, which may usher in a populist leader. Germany is set to be the largest gross issuer of debt among euro area peers next year, according to strategists at Commerzbank AG, who estimate the region as a whole could sell a record amount in excess of €1.5 trillion.

--With assistance from James Hirai, Abraham Gonzalez and 'Tofe Ayeni.

news.Title: NYC lawmakers weigh compromise on Amazon delivery worker bill, Bloomberg reports
news.Content:
Investing.com -- New York City lawmakers are weighing substantial revisions to proposed legislation that would force Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) to directly employ thousands of outsourced delivery drivers, according to a Bloomberg report. The potential overhaul signals a strategic compromise in a high-stakes regulatory battle pitting the e-commerce giant against Mayor Zohran Mamdani and a City Council majority.

Under the revised framework, lawmakers are considering replacing the strict direct-hire mandate of the Delivery Protection Act with a tiered menu of operational options, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Amazon would be permitted to either bring drivers onto its own payroll, rely on established carriers such as UPS or the U.S. Postal Service, or continue contracting with roughly 40 local third-party delivery service partners.

Retaining the third-party subcontractor model, however, would require a fundamental transformation of Amazon's current logistics oversight. To qualify as truly independent operators, contracted delivery firms would have to be freed from Amazon's control over daily delivery quotas, routing, and personnel decisions including hiring and discipline, while subjecting those business relationships to heightened municipal scrutiny.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

The legislative shift follows a fracture in the opposition coalition originally bankrolled by Amazon to fight the bill. While small business delivery partners initially warned the direct-hire mandate would shutter their operations, several owners broke ranks to hold independent talks with city officials, pressing for transparency into Amazon's routing algorithms and regulatory protections against their overwhelming dependence on the tech giant.

Against that backdrop, Amazon had previously threatened to pull its logistics infrastructure out of New York City entirely if forced to absorb the courier workforce. For its part, the company indicated it remains engaged with City Council Speaker Julie Menin's office to reach a workable outcome, while Menin's office noted that a range of options remains under active consideration to balance worker protections, jobs, and street safety.

Story Continues

Even without the direct-hire requirement, the revised legislation would impose new regulatory hurdles on last-mile logistics operators. Amazon and competing delivery networks would be required to obtain licenses from the city's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, empowering the agency to investigate complaints and enforce safety standards ahead of a potential council vote in the coming weeks.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 19: Stock Market Today, Nov. 19: Alphabet Shares Fall as Anthropic Nasdaq Debut Puts Fresh Value on Google's Stake
news.Content:
Wall Street's early rally unraveled on Thursday, November 19, as even the largest initial public offering in history proved insufficient to restore investor confidence. Despite Anthropic's (NASDAQ:ANT) successful stock market debut, selling pressure intensified throughout the session as concerns surrounding elevated valuations and the prospect of further interest rate hikes continued to weigh on equities.

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 2.00% to 7,177, marking its sixth consecutive session of losses and its longest losing streak since April 2024. The Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) reversed its early gains, closing 2.23% lower at 23,886, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) plunged more than 1,100 points, falling 2.19% to 49,097.

Selling pressure extended beyond equities, with December gold futures settling 1.50% lower at $3,685.50, while the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.05%. All 11 S&P 500 sectors finished in negative territory, with consumer discretionary leading losses at 2.79%.

Today's biggest moves

Despite the broader market sell-off, Insmed (NASDAQ:INSM) surged 20.58% following reports that French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi (NASDAQ:SNY) is considering acquiring the biotechnology company. Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) was the S&P 500's best-performing stock, gaining 6.42% after reporting strong quarterly results and raising its fiscal 2027 outlook.

Conversely, Williams-Sonoma (NYSE:WSM) was the S&P 500's worst-performing stock, plunging 15.16% following its quarterly earnings report. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) fell 7.72% following a report from investigative outlet Hunterbrook alleging ties to a blacklisted Chinese server manufacturer.

What this means for investors

Anthropic's record-breaking IPO demonstrates that investor appetite for artificial intelligence (AI) remains substantial, even as concerns surrounding technology valuations intensify. However, the sheer size of Anthropic's offering also raises questions about how much capital remains available to support other AI investments.

With technology companies competing for financing to fund increasingly expensive infrastructure projects, elevated interest rates could force investors to become more selective about which businesses warrant premium valuations.

Perhaps more concerning is the deterioration in market breadth over the past week. Selling pressure is no longer confined to high-growth technology stocks, suggesting that investor concerns are shifting toward the broader economic outlook. With the Federal Reserve signaling that additional interest rate hikes may be necessary, upcoming inflation and employment data could prove particularly influential in determining the market's direction.

Story Continues

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

news.Title: Morgan Stanley’s Vintage Values 2027: 5 Stocks Analysts See Climbing Further
news.Content:
Bloomberg reported on November 13, 2026, that one bank's strategists expect the S&P 500 to reach 8,700 within 12 months. They also see earnings growth slowing to 11% in 2027 from 36% in 2026. That gap matters because slower profit growth changes what investors reward. According to the report, buyers are willing to pay up for companies that keep growing, because growth is becoming harder to find. For stock pickers, that raises the value of any name where earnings momentum is still intact. It matters most when the market has not yet priced all of it in.

Slower Profit Growth Raises the Bar

On November 13, 2026, chip stocks sold off and the S&P 500 fell 0.4%, although it still gained about 2.5% on the week, according to Yahoo Finance's market coverage. Wholesale inflation also reached its highest annual rate in nearly four years, and the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.15% on November 13, 2026. Higher yields make future earnings worth less today. That is one reason the largest technology companies have drawn scrutiny, since their spending has pushed free cash flow negative. Even so, Bloomberg's report described them as "relatively defensive." Readers who want a broader look at the rebound case can see our ranking of oversold AI stocks where Wall Street analysts see big upside .

What a Price Target Really Means

A price target is an analyst's estimate of where a stock should trade in about 12 months, built from forecasts for earnings, growth and a reasonable valuation multiple. Upside is simply the gap between today's share price and the average of those targets, expressed as a percentage. Because targets are opinions rather than guarantees, they can move quickly after a company reports, and a cut does not always mean the analyst has turned negative. Sometimes a firm trims its target to reflect a stock that has already risen, or an expectations bar that was set too high, while keeping a positive rating.

That is why the rating and the target are best read together. An upgrade with a lower target tells a different story from a reiterated rating with a higher one. The reasons behind a change, such as delayed contracts, better cost control or a pricing shift, usually say more than the number does. Ranking by average upside adds a second layer. A large gap to the average target can point to a stock that has fallen out of favor as easily as to one analysts expect to take off. Our list of NYSE-listed stocks with large analyst-estimated upside shows how wide that spread can get on a single exchange. Following the reasons as well as the numbers keeps that distinction clear.

Story Continues

We shared the expanded list of Morgan Stanley's Vintage Values 2027: 10 Stocks Analysts See Climbing Further here. You can find the top 5 stocks below.

Our Methodology

To compile this list, we looked at the 15 US-listed stocks in Morgan Stanley's Vintage Values 2027 portfolio and ranked them by average upside potential, based on analysts' average price target. We then picked the 10 with the highest upside that had a full year of share price history and a positive share price performance over that period, and counted the list down from there. We also list each stock's market cap and its share price performance over the past year.

Note: All data was sourced on November 16, 2026.

At Insider Monkey, we are obsessed with what hedge funds do. The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

Morgan Stanley's Vintage Values 2027: 5 Stocks Analysts See Climbing Further

5. Equinix (NASDAQ: EQIX )

Market Cap: $104.31 billion

Average Upside Potential: 17%

1-Year Performance: 34.14%

Raymond James reiterated its Strong Buy rating on Equinix on October 29, 2026, with a $1,250 price target. The firm pointed to the raised guidance and to pricing about 12% higher on new deployments. Equinix is a digital infrastructure company that operates data centers where businesses connect their networks and cloud services.

The company released results for the third quarter of 2026 on October 28, 2026. Revenue rose 11% to $2.571 billion, and record annualized gross bookings reached $533 million, up 35%. It was the third consecutive time Equinix raised its full-year 2026 guidance. Chief Executive Officer Adaire Fox-Martin said the results reflect the company's growing importance, citing double-digit growth in interconnection and monthly recurring revenue.

Equinix is also moving faster on supply, planning many more cabinets for delivery in 2026 than first anticipated. It introduced Fabric One, a connectivity service for distributed cloud, network and AI environments, along with an inference exchange built with partners. It also completed its investment in atNorth, which expands its Nordic footprint with high-density capacity powered by renewable energy. The company's path from a 1998 data center operator to an AI player is told in our earlier profile of Equinix .

4. Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN )

Market Cap: $2.86 trillion

Average Upside Potential: 24%

1-Year Performance: 12.66%

Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak lowered his price target on Amazon to $335 from $350 on October 30, 2026, and kept an Overweight rating. The reason was about expectations, not weakness. Amazon Web Services added about $3.8 billion in revenue from the second quarter to the third. That was the second-largest increase in its history, yet it fell short of what investors hoped to see. Amazon is an online retailer that also owns Amazon Web Services, its cloud business.

The company released results for the third quarter of 2026 on October 29, 2026. AWS revenue grew 39%, its fastest pace in nearly five years, and total operating income reached $28.1 billion at the highest operating margin Amazon has reported. Earnings per share came in a little below analyst estimates.

Chief Executive Officer Andy Jassy said AWS is projected to grow more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028. He added that broader selection and faster delivery are helping Amazon win retail share with improving margins. He also pointed to newer businesses, from grocery and pharmacy to Zoox, as progressing encouragingly. Our piece on whether Amazon's cash engines can fund its robotaxi bet picks up that thread.

3. Williams Companies (NYSE: WMB )

Market Cap: $86.36 billion

Average Upside Potential: 25%

1-Year Performance: 13.26%

Goldman Sachs kept a Buy rating on Williams on November 12, 2026, while lowering its price target to $82 from $84. Williams is an energy infrastructure company built around natural gas pipelines, storage and gathering.

The cut followed Williams' third-quarter 2026 results, released on November 2, 2026. Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% to $2.039 billion and adjusted earnings per share climbed 10%. The company said it is tracking toward the upper half of its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range. Cash generation also improved, and the dividend was covered by a comfortable margin on an available-funds basis.

Growth projects continue to arrive. Williams closed its acquisition of Momentum Midstream on September 3, 2026, which strengthens its Haynesville position for LNG, industrial and power demand. It announced a storage expansion at Clay Basin and expects its Plato North power project to be in service by mid-November. Chief Executive Officer Chad Zamarin has targeted adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 11% a year through 2030. That gives the Buy case a clear growth target to measure against, and the dividend remains well covered by cash flow. For more on what protects those returns, see our look at the company's economic moat .

2. Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL )

Market Cap: $3.57 trillion

Average Upside Potential: 33%

1-Year Performance: 6.28%

BMO Capital Markets cut its price target on Alphabet to $425 from $480 on October 29, 2026, while keeping its Outperform rating. Alphabet is the holding company behind Google Services, Google Cloud and Other Bets, the group that houses its longer-term projects.

The cut came a day after the company released results for the third quarter of 2026 on October 28, 2026. Revenue reached $127.6 billion, and Google Cloud revenue grew 103%, with its backlog standing at $561 billion. Search revenue growth of 12% was below what at least one other firm had modeled.

Chief Executive Officer Sundar Pichai said Alphabet is now on a half-trillion-dollar annual revenue run rate. He said the Gemini app has reached one billion users, which he called the fastest-growing product in Google's history, and that Search query growth is the highest in five years. Subscriptions, platforms and devices revenue grew, driven by YouTube subscriptions and demand for AI plans in Google One. Pichai added that usage of the new Gemini 4 model ramped up three-and-a-half times faster than Gemini 3 in its first week, even with capacity constraints. We also examined whether Alphabet's valuation reflects Waymo's potential in a separate piece.

1. Keysight Technologies (NYSE: KEYS )

Market Cap: $48.55 billion

Average Upside Potential: 49%

1-Year Performance: 59.28%

Goldman Sachs analyst Mark Delaney raised his price target on Keysight to $487 from $452 on October 6, 2026, and kept a Buy rating, pointing to strong demand for AI infrastructure. Keysight makes the electronic design and test equipment that engineers use to check chips, data centers and communications networks.

The company reported results for its fiscal third quarter, ended July 31, 2026, on August 18, 2026. Revenue rose 36% to $1.85 billion, and non-GAAP earnings per share reached $3.07. Growth came across both segments, led by commercial communications, where demand tied to AI data centers was strongest. Orders grew faster than revenue, and free cash flow rose from a year earlier. Management raised its outlook for the fourth quarter and the full year, though it noted supply constraints. Chief Executive Officer Satish Dhanasekaran said the record results reflect the growing relevance of the company's strategy and portfolio.

Keysight is expected to report its next quarterly results on November 19, 2026, and analysts expect earnings of $3.37 per share. Whether AI-driven demand keeps this pace is the question for that report. Our look at whether AI testing is becoming a durable growth engine explores it.

news.Content:
The 13F holdings of hedge funds for Q3 are available, which means you can track and analyze the smart money moves made in Q3. One such move Dan Loeb's Third Point LLC made was to exit its Amazon (AMZN) stake, as per its recent 13F filing.

Dan Loeb is a hedge fund manager and the founder and CEO of Third Point LLC. Founded with a few million dollars three decades ago, the hedge fund manages around $29 billion in total assets today.

According to a Seeking Alpha report, the filing shows Third Point divested 1.75 million Amazon shares in the third quarter and exited the position entirely. It also exited positions in Warner Brothers Discovery ahead of Paramount Skydance's (SKYD) acquisition, and trimmed its stake in Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG).

Where Third Point Invested in Q3 of 2026

The fund opened three new positions, according to Seeking Alpha. It purchased 655,000 shares worth $475 million of Meta (META), five million shares worth $438.7 million of Unum (UNM), and 1.50 million shares worth $342.6 million of Nvidia (NVDA).

The report also states the hedge fund added to existing bets. Its SpaceX (SPCX) stake grew to 980,400 shares, worth $147.9 million, an increase of almost 5x compared to the last quarter.

Its position in Ares Management (ARES) rose to 1.16 million shares from 375,000, while it held 4.94 million shares of API Group (APG), up from 2.87 million.

Amazon was not a small position in the fund's Q2 portfolio. As of June 30, it ranked among Third Point's largest holdings, along with Warner Brothers Discovery and Alphabet, according to Quiver Quant.

The fund exited positions in two stocks and reduced its stake in Alphabet. However, it still has exposure to tech stocks, given a higher stake in Nvidia and Meta.

How Amazon Performed in Q3 of 2026?

Amazon reported revenue of $202 billion in Q3, an increase of 12% year over year. Comparatively, operating income grew by 61% to $28.1 billion, indicating a margin of 13.9%, a company record.

The cloud segment, Amazon Web Services (AWS), grew at a much faster pace. It reported revenue of $46 billion, up 39.3% YoY. CEO Andy Jassy said sales growth has accelerated for six consecutive quarters and at the fastest pace since 2021. AWS also earned $17.8 billion in operating income, which translates to a margin of 38.7%. Moreover, AWS ended Q3 with a backlog of $578 billion.

Story Continues

Jassy claimed, "We're installing an AI accelerator about every 14 seconds," he said.

In the retail business:

North America revenue rose 6% to $112.9 billion.

Operating income stood at $8.7 billion.

International revenue grew 8% to $43.1 billion.

Amazon also pointed to a calendar quirk. Prime Day moved into the second quarter this year, which cut Q3 growth by 400 basis points.

AWS is Key for Amazon

Jassy made a bold claim and said AWS can grow north of 40% in both 2027 and 2028. He added it could become a $1 trillion revenue business in five to 10 years. However, Amazon spent $75.9 billion in capital spending in Q3 and expects capex at $220 billion in 2026. This spending could be meaningfully higher in 2027.

AI services earn lower margins than core cloud services, while higher component prices are also a headwind. So, investors should expect AWS margins to move around from quarter to quarter.

Amazon guided fourth-quarter sales to between $240 billion and $247 billion and expects operating income of $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion.

What Third Point's Exit Means for Investors

Dan Loeb could be wary of rising capital expenditures for Amazon over the next 15 months. In fact, the e-commerce giant is projected to report a free cash outflow of $41 billion in 2025 and $24 billion in 2026.

However, adjusted earnings per share are projected to expand from $7.17 in 2025 to $20.89 in 2030. So, if AMZN stock is priced at 26x, which is similar to the current multiple, it could double within the next three years.

Out of the 56 analysts covering AMZN stock, 48 recommend "Strong Buy," five recommend "Moderate Buy," and three recommend "Hold." The average AMZN stock price target is $328, above the current price of $268.

One fund's sale is not a verdict on Amazon. The filing shows what Third Point held on Sept. 30, but does not explain why the stake was exited. A fund founded by Dan Loeb walked away from Amazon in a quarter when the company was about to post record margins and its fastest cloud growth in nearly five years.

Amazon is spending heavily, which should drive future earnings and cash flow higher, allowing it to deliver outsized gains after years of underperformance.

news.Title: NYC Lawmakers Weigh Overhaul of Amazon Delivery Worker Bill
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- New York City lawmakers are in discussions to modify a mandate that would require Amazon.com Inc. to directly hire thousands of delivery workers under a bill that has pitted the company against Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Modi Tries to End Trump Photo-Op in Awkward Viral Moment

Costco Shoppers Are Panic-Buying Due to Outages, Analysts Say

Iran Hit Key Infrastructure, Isn't Behind Tech Outages, US Says

Anthropic Raises $107.3 Billion to Top SpaceX's Record Debut

Anthropic IPO Allocates Nothing to Most Institutional Orders

The lawmakers are considering replacing the direct hire mandate with a menu of options, allowing Amazon to either directly employ the workers, use carriers like UPS or the US Postal Service, or contract with fully independent third-party operators, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

For the delivery companies, it would require a complete change from their current operating model, one of the people said. Amazon would have to give up oversight of the contracted companies, including control of their routes, daily delivery quotas, hiring, firing and disciplining employees, the people said.

The proposed revisions would represent a compromise on legislation that sought to reshape the delivery industry by requiring companies such as Amazon to bring workers employed by subcontractors onto their own payrolls. Under the changes being considered, Amazon could continue using its network of small business delivery partners but would have to grant them autonomy and come under greater city oversight of those relationships.

If an agreement is reached, the legislation could come up for a vote within a few weeks, according to the people.

"We've made clear we're willing to work with anyone who wants to make progress on this matter," said Amazon spokesperson Steve Kelly. "We appreciate that Speaker Julie Menin has met with numerous stakeholders on this bill, including us, and we'll remain engaged with her and her team as work on the bill continues to try and reach the best outcome for New Yorkers."

In a statement, a Menin spokesperson, Jack Lobel, said her office is "working around the clock with the bill sponsor and stakeholders to achieve legislation that protects workers, jobs, and street safety. A range of options are still on the table."

The bill, called the Delivery Protection Act, has gained the backing of an overwhelming majority of City Council members and Mamdani.

Initially, Amazon and the small business owners presented a united front against the bill. Amazon bankrolled a lobbying group that included many of its delivery partners, which also opposed the legislation.

Story Continues

That alliance began to fracture when some business owners started meeting independently with city officials, according to a person familiar with the negotiations who asked not to be identified discussing private talks. The owners sought greater transparency into how Amazon sets delivery routes and determines how many packages drivers are expected to handle during a shift.

The meetings marked a breakthrough in the negotiations, the person said. The business owners began pressing City Council members for protections from requirements imposed by Amazon, arguing that their dependence on the company left them with little leverage. They ultimately persuaded the bill's sponsors that the small businesses, not just their drivers, also needed protections from Amazon, the person said.

Amazon has threatened to pull its logistics operations out of the city if it is required to directly employ all of its delivery workers, as the bill currently proposes. Its backers say outsourced workers endure unsafe conditions while Amazon reaps the benefit of lower cost labor.

There are about 40 Amazon delivery service partners, small businesses that hire couriers to handle Amazon packages, operating in the city. Many of the small business owners opposed the bill, saying it would put them out of business.

While the changes would remove a key provision of the bill, it would still require Amazon and other companies operating last-mile delivery facilities to be licensed by the city's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, which would investigate complaints and ensure safety standards are met.

news.Title: Google selects Blue Origin’s New Glenn for Project Suncatcher
news.Content:
Blue Origin and Google have entered into a launch services agreement for Project Suncatcher, Google's research moonshot exploring how an interconnected network of solar-powered satellites equipped with its AI chips, Tensor Processing Units, could scale machine learning compute in space, the companies announced. The launch, targeted for the first quarter of 2029, will be Google's first dedicated heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher. The mission is designed to deploy satellites – each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack – into sun-synchronous orbit, marking a milestone in Google's research to scale machine learning compute in space. "Project Suncatcher represents the ambitious missions New Glenn was built to support. Its heavy-lift capacity and large payload volume give customers the flexibility to bring new capabilities to orbit. We're proud to work with Google to explore space-based computing and its potential to expand the space economy," said Jordan Charles, Senior Vice President of New Glenn at Blue Origin.

news.Title: Stanley Druckenmiller dumps entire $120M Alphabet stake to buy gold mining stock
news.Content:
I've had trades where price moves toward my take-profit, hits it, and then reverses almost immediately. It can feel as though the market was waiting for your exit before turning in the opposite direction. As a trader, I know how satisfying a well-timed exit can feel, especially when you avoid the reversal by a few ticks.

Druckenmiller's latest filing has a similar twist. Imagine selling every share of a company you own, only to watch it report its first earnings miss in three years shortly afterward. The timing looks almost like a sniper exit. And this makes his latest move worth a closer look.

Also Read: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller reveals his next investment

The Duquesne Family Office held 336,300 shares of Alphabet (GOOGL), valued at $120.2 million, on June 30 as indicated in its Q2 13F filing . By Sept. 30, it held none, according to its Q3 13F filing , filed Nov. 16. In their place, Duquesne opened new positions in gold miners, including a 380,400-share stake in Newmont (NEM) valued at $43.9 million.

A 13F is like a snapshot, not the entire diary. It shows what was held on the last day of the quarter, and nothing about trade dates, prices paid, or reasons. So the story is worth reading carefully before you try to copy it.

What Duquesne's filing shows, and what it hides

The exit was complete within one reporting window. That is notable for a firm of Duquesne's stature. Still, the filing does not tell us when Druckenmiller sold or at what price. The dollar figures reflect the value of the holdings at the close of the Q2 quarter, not what he paid.

The new positions also include Barrick Mining (B), Somnigroup International Inc. ( SGI) and Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM), according to the filing. Taken together, the gold stakes are a small slice of Duquesne's book. My read is that they are too small to count as a big macro call on bullion.

What happened to Alphabet after the snapshot

Duquesne's Sept. 30 picture came before Alphabet's Oct. 28 third-quarter report , which ended a 12-quarter streak of earnings beats. GAAP earnings per share (EPS) of $2.12 missed the $2.97 consensus, according to the company's results. An $8.70 billion loss on equity securities cut diluted EPS by $0.55.

Let's go further and look at spending. Capital expenditures hit $51.4 billion, up 114.4%. This left free cash flow at -$9.1 billion, according to the company's Q3 results . It was also negative $5.9 billion in the prior Q2 quarter . Alphabet funded part of the buildout with $28.7 billion in senior notes and raised $12 billion through an at-the-market share offering, mainly to cover taxes on employee equity grants.

Story Continues

More Investors:

Bill Ackman's $14 billion bet beyond the Magnificent 7

Legendary fund manager builds $172 million stake in mega-cap tech stock

Peter Thiel makes new $161 million ETF bet, dethroning Amazon stock

The business itself is still growing fast. Revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion. Google Cloud revenue climbed 103% to $30.7 billion, and Cloud operating income reached $11.1 billion, up from $3.6 billion a year earlier. The Gemini app reached 1 billion users.

Currently, GOOGL trades at $279.20, down 17% over the past month and 10.85% year-to-date. That is about 14 times trailing earnings, though the multiple appears low partly due to a $99.0 billion second-quarter gain on equity securities.

Why Newmont caught Druckenmiller's eye, maybe

Newmont is the world's largest gold miner. It reported third-quarter revenue of $6.36 billion, up 15.2%, and adjusted EPS of $2.20, beating the $1.94 estimate, according to a company statement . Free cash flow was $1.9 billion. The company holds $8.83 billion in cash against $5.58 billion in debt.

CEO Natascha Viljoen said Newmont remains on track for its full-year production guidance. It has returned $1.9 billion to shareholders since its last earnings call, and has shrunk its share count by about 10% since February 2024.

Related: 91-year-old investor sees healthcare titan doubling in 3 years

The realized gold price averaged $4,317 an ounce in the quarter. Management warned that unit costs should experience cost escalation in 2027.

NEM shares closed at $104.53 on Nov. 18, down 6% that day, after hitting a high of $135.29 in August. The stock is up 5.36% year-to-date and 21.84% over the past year. Miners swing sharply with bullion, the dollar, and Treasury yields.

My verdict: study the thesis, skip the copycat trade

I would treat this as a prompt to stress-test your own Alphabet position, not as a signal to sell. Free cash flow has been negative for two straight quarters, and Alphabet's next capital spending update and Cloud margins will matter far more than a week-old filing.

Cloud revenue doubled. Cash burn doubled too. That tension is what a thoughtful investor should be weighing.

Copying the trade adds little. The date, price, and reasoning are all hidden, and the gold stakes are small. Druckenmiller may be hedging, rotating, or simply taking profit. The filing cannot tell us which.

Investing.com — The AI chip trade has unraveled this month. Intel's weak forecast set off a broad semiconductor sell-off, and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) had already slid about 22% between the first reports of its $115 billion bid for Lumentum and the deal's announcement. Even Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE)—the laser maker supplying the optical links inside AI data centers—has plunged 34.0% over the past month to $551.07, including an 11.8% slide in the past week alone.

The headline growth is what makes Lumentum tempting, but the stock no longer trades on its own results. Analysts forecast 121.5% revenue growth and 130.6% EPS growth, yet Marvell's all-stock agreement pays Lumentum shareholders a fixed 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own, so every slide in Marvell now lands directly on Lumentum's price. GAAP earnings also remain negative at -7.6 times trailing earnings, and InvestingPro's valuation models rate the stock merely "Fair" at $566.14, just 2.7% above the share price. That leaves dip-buyers taking on Marvell's swings without a valuation cushion of their own.

The Laser Supplier AI Cannot Get Enough Of

Lumentum makes its money selling the lasers and optical components that carry data between AI servers, and it sells them into a market where demand has outrun supply. It holds dominant share in indium phosphide lasers and high-speed EMLs, commands 70% to 80% of the pump laser market, and is the only merchant supplier of optical circuit switches with a proven shipping track record. Pump laser shipments surged more than 80% year-over-year, backed by three-year take-or-pay agreements with major hyperscalers.

Fiscal fourth-quarter results showed how much that position now earns. Revenue surged 109% year-over-year and 23% sequentially to $1.01 billion, the eighth straight quarter of growth, while non-GAAP gross margin topped 50% for the first time and non-GAAP operating margin expanded 2,160 basis points to 36.6%. The first quarter of fiscal 2027 then beat estimates, with revenue climbing 136.5% year-over-year to $1.26 billion and EPS of $4.57.

Story Continues

The negative trailing multiple stems from a single accounting charge rather than weak operations. A one-time, non-cash $7.8 billion charge from converting convertible debt into equity produced a fourth-quarter GAAP net loss of $7.2 billion, yet first-quarter GAAP net income reached $360.3 million.

Wall Street Cools, Fair Value Holds the Line

Wall Street has turned more cautious since the deal. B. Riley cut Lumentum to Neutral with a $770 target, Stifel moved to Hold at $806, and UBS holds at $686, while Bernstein SocGen still rates it a Buy at $700. Every one of those targets sits above the current share price, and the average analyst target of roughly $1,070 sits far higher. Estimates keep climbing: 16 analysts have revised EPS forecasts higher over the past 90 days with none lower, and consensus calls for $28.41 in fiscal 2027 and $45.84 in fiscal 2028.

InvestingPro's Fair Value models see far less room to run, placing intrinsic value at $566.14 per share—just 2.7% above the share price and well below the Street's average target.

The main risk is that Lumentum's fate is no longer its own. Marvell's slide has already reduced the implied deal value from the roughly $1,132 per share it carried at announcement, and closing is not expected until the first half of 2028, subject to stockholder and regulatory approvals that could include China. Investor-rights firms have launched investigations into whether the ratio fairly values Lumentum shareholders, and insiders sold about $86 million of stock in the three months before the announcement.

A Growth Story on Someone Else's Clock

Investing.com — Big Tech's AI spending race has become a funding question this autumn, as investors weigh how much of the data center build-out the largest platforms can pay for from their own cash. Even Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) has slipped 4.3% over the past month. Yet Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META)—the owner of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp—has fared far worse, dropping 12.6% over the past month to $616.38, including a 1.2% slip in the past week.

On paper, Meta looks like the one Big Tech stock that didn't get caught in a valuation bubble, but its low multiple hides an AI bill that has already pushed free cash flow below zero. Shares trade at just 20.9 times trailing earnings with a 0.3% dividend yield, while analysts forecast 27.8% revenue growth and 25.8% EPS growth. Even so, InvestingPro's valuation models refuse to call it a bargain, rating shares merely "Fair" at $656.50, just 6.5% above the current price, because escalating AI infrastructure capex is eating into free cash flow.

Recognizing when a headline multiple hides a cash-flow squeeze is what ProPicks AI is built for. In Tech Titans, InvestingPro's strategy dedicated to high-margin tech leaders, Meta was passed over, with the strategy looking past its 21x multiple and mega-cap capex bloat to hold leaner semiconductor equipment and cloud infrastructure plays that convert revenue directly into cash.

See the cash-generative tech leaders Tech Titans holds instead: Explore the Tech Titans strategy on InvestingPro

More Users, Higher Ad Prices

Meta makes its money selling advertising against the attention of the world's largest family of social media and messaging apps, and its moat is pricing power at that scale. Daily active people across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, and Threads reached an all-time high of 3.64 billion in the third quarter, with record time spent on Instagram and Facebook. Advertisers paid more to reach them: ad impressions rose 10% year-over-year while the average price per ad climbed 14%.

Third-quarter results proved that pricing power is intact. Revenue surged 26% year-over-year to $64.6 billion, topping the $63.34 billion forecast, and EPS of $3.83 beat the $3.57 consensus by 7.3%. Advertising revenue climbed 26% to $63.1 billion, partnership ads passed a $15 billion annual run rate after growing 97%, and management guided fourth-quarter revenue to $73 billion to $76 billion.

Story Continues

The cash is still coming in—operating cash flow reached $32.8 billion in the quarter—but it no longer covers the build-out. Capital spending of $34.9 billion pushed free cash flow to negative $2.1 billion, Meta's first quarterly cash burn in over a decade, against positive $10.63 billion a year earlier.

The Street Sees a Bargain, the Cash Flow Does Not

Wall Street sees the dip as an opportunity. UBS reiterated a Buy with an $815 target on November 17, Wells Fargo rates the stock Overweight at $995, and Truist sits at $1,000, while Scotiabank is the cautious voice with a Hold at $650. The median price target of $848.23 sits far above the current share price. On forward estimates the multiple falls from 21.2 times fiscal 2026 earnings to 17.6 times fiscal 2027, and a PEG ratio of 0.71 shows a stock priced at a discount to its growth.

InvestingPro's Fair Value models take a far more conservative line, placing intrinsic value at $656.50 per share—6.5% above the current price but well below the Street's median target. On that measure, the sell-off has brought Meta to fair value rather than below it.

The main risk is that the AI bill keeps growing faster than the cash to pay for it. Meta has narrowed full-year 2026 capex guidance to $135 billion to $145 billion, Wells Fargo expects fiscal 2027 capex of roughly $250 billion, and management declined to give fiscal 2027 guidance before the fourth-quarter call. To fund the gap, Meta announced a record $97.5 billion equity financing plan, including $25 billion of common stock priced at $625 per share and up to $60 billion of new non-voting Class C shares sold over time from early 2027. Nvidia and AMD committed $3 billion and $1 billion as cornerstone investors, but the scale of the raise leaves existing shareholders facing meaningful dilution.

Before buying a 21x P/E Big Tech dip, investors must weigh Meta's advertising pricing power against an AI build-out that has pushed free cash flow negative and opened the door to heavy dilution. A Cheap Multiple With an Expensive Bill

Meta has shown that its advertising business can still raise prices and grow at enormous scale. Until the AI build-out starts paying for itself instead of being funded with new shares, the low P/E is the market's price for that bill rather than a discount it has overlooked.

news.Title: Nebius Stock’s (NBIS) Q3 Sell-Off Looks Like an Opportunity
news.Content: Nebius (NBIS) stock's Q3 sell-off looks like an attractive opportunity, with shares down almost 64% from their 52-week high. The artificial intelligence (AI) cloud infrastructure provider disappointed investors with another capacity delay, but the underlying business momentum tells a very different story. Rather than pulling back, customers are locking in much larger, multi-year commitments. As CEO Arkady Volozh emphasized on the earnings call, "The demand for AI is real and substantial." Q3 2026 revenue surged 571%, and new contract economics improved. I understand the concerns about financing this enormous expansion. Yet customers' willingness to help fund it makes me more confident. Thus, I rate NBIS stock a Buy . A Strong Quarter Got Overshadowed Nebius' strong Q3 results got overshadowed by another capacity delay. Investors were already questioning Neocloud financing and the sustainability of AI spending. Nebius then shifted some expected revenue into early 2027 because third-party capacity was delayed. Management now expects 2026 revenue near the low end of its $3.0–$3.4 billion range. Promotion BLACK FRIDAY SALE Get 75% Off TipRanks Premium and unlock powerful investing tools to make smarter, more confident investment decisions Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks Learn more about TipRanks Premium Its $7 billion-plus annualized revenue milestone moves from December to February. That is disappointing, although the customer contracts behind the delayed capacity remain intact. More importantly, the company showed considerable progress. Revenue reached $980.8 million, up 68% sequentially, while AI Cloud revenue grew 643% year-over-year . Group adjusted EBITDA reached $465.8 million , and AI Cloud's adjusted EBITDA margin was 53.2%. Annualized revenue run rate rose 113% sequentially to $6.4 billion. Q3 included $325 million of nonrecurring partner revenue. Excluding that contribution, revenue still exceeded four times last year's total. Customers have also signed over $12 billion of contract value since Q3 began. The improving contract terms are what impressed me most. Prepayments on Q3 contracts lasting at least a year covered more than 100% of associated capex. That compares with 50%–60% in Q2. Management's revenue-based payback estimate for comparable contracts improved to 19 months from 22 months. Customers are signing longer agreements at higher prices, helping Nebius recover its spending faster. Story Continues I believe this is really important for a company buying expensive graphics processing units (GPUs). Customer funding reduces its dependence on the next debt deal or equity raise. The Growth Outlook Still Looks Excellent Meanwhile, the growth outlook still looks excellent heading into 2027. Management expects $12–$13 billion of revenue , roughly four times this year's level. Four new sites began generating revenue in Q3, with more capacity arriving during Q4. Nebius plans to add over 1 GW annually, increasingly through owned sites. That should give it more control over delivery and operating costs. Management expects prepayments and investment-grade contract financing to cover 75%–85% of 2027's $40–$45 billion capex. Microsoft (MSFT) and Meta (META) agreements support that financing strategy. Nebius has over $40 billion of similar committed revenue and ended Q3 with $7.4 billion in cash. Nvidia's (NVDA) results on November 17 further strengthened my confidence in that outlook. The chipmaker's Data Center revenue grew 110%, and Rubin achieved Nvidia's fastest product ramp. Nebius was among the providers already running Rubin racks. Nvidia also described extraordinary neocloud demand, with $32 billion of commitments extending into 2032 and beyond. Its support depends on financing being secured and capacity becoming operational. I see those conditions as sensible discipline. They require projects to work before Nvidia's commitments take effect. So they don't suggest customers have stopped wanting compute. Rental pricing offers further evidence. Nebius raised selected on-demand GPU rates roughly 17%–21% from October 1. Across Nvidia's customer base, some Hopper contracts renewed at up to twice the prior price. B300 rental rates have risen over 60% since introduction. Higher prices on heavily used equipment improve the potential return on each installed dollar. Nebius is also building services on top of GPU rentals. Token Factory approaches a multi-hundred-million-dollar revenue run rate, with contract value increasing 17-fold sequentially. Managed inference gives existing customers another reason to spend on its platform. Over time, that could make the business more valuable than a basic compute rental operation. NBIS' Earnings Could Catch Up Quickly The market is struggling to value Nebius stock, but I believe earnings could catch up quickly if the company delivers the planned expansion. The stock is now trading at 36x consensus 2028 earnings per share (EPS) of $2.95 . That falls to 15.7x 2029 EPS of $6.80. Losses expected through 2027 make today's P/E less useful. The question is whether new capacity can produce the profits those later estimates imply. Management targets pre-tax breakeven in Q4 2027. I think that rising rental prices and stronger prepayments make that goal more credible to me. Its full-stack cloud platform also provides ways to earn more from existing customers. If revenue reaches $12-$13 billion next year, earnings could scale rapidly as infrastructure fills. I consider Nebius one of the better-positioned neoclouds for that transition. Of course, the risks remain substantial. Further construction delays could increase financing needs and dilution. Large customers account for considerable revenue, while GPU replacement costs will consume cash. Customer advances bring future service obligations, and EBITDA excludes depreciation and financing costs. An eventual supply glut could also reverse today's pricing gains. This is a speculative investment, but Q3 gave me stronger reasons to accept those risks. Is NBIS Stock a Buy? Wall Street rates NBIS a Moderate Buy, based on nine Buys, two Holds, and one Sell. The $260.90 average price target implies about 144% upside. Several analysts lowered their targets after Q3, reflecting the delivery setback. Conclusion Nebius still needs to bring capacity online on schedule. Meanwhile, customers are committing more money upfront and accepting higher prices. That is encouraging evidence for both demand and future profitability. I think the sell-off gives investors an attractive opportunity, provided they can tolerate the risks of this enormous buildout. news.Title: 3 Dirt Cheap Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks to Load Up on Before 2027
news.Content:
Many investors and analysts still aren't convinced that the artificial intelligence (AI) industry will continue expanding rapidly. That's partly why some AI companies, particularly those spending a small fortune on capex, haven't performed that well this year. But what if Wall Street is wrong and the AI market maintains its recent momentum over the medium term? In my view, there is a good chance that will happen. And if it does, several AI stocks could be great bargain buys right now. Let's consider three of them: Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU).

Image source: Getty Images.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

1. Alphabet

Alphabet's shares are down 11% this year. Investors are worried about the company's capex and declining free cash flow, which has been negative for two straight quarters. However, Alphabet's AI-related investments are paying off. The company's core advertising business remains strong, and cloud computing sales continue to accelerate.

In the third quarter, Alphabet's total revenue came in at $127.6 billion, up 25% year over year. The company's Google Cloud sales were $30.7 billion, up 103% compared to the year-ago period. The tech leader's earnings per share declined to $2.12, down from $2.87, while its free cash flow was a negative $9.1 billion.

That said, Alphabet ended the quarter with $561 billion in cloud backlog, up 262% year over year -- and it expects to recognize 55% of it, or $308.55 billion, over the next 24 months. The company will likely receive new orders as well. That suggests Alphabet's cloud sales could continue to grow at a good clip in the foreseeable future, especially given the AI industry's continued growth.

The near-term negative free cash flow is worth the massive opportunities Alphabet is tapping into. The stock may have lagged broader equities this year, but Alphabet's prospects look bright from current levels. The company's price/earnings-to-growth (PEG) ratio of 0.5 is well within the undervalued range, which typically starts below 1.

2. Amazon

Amazon has remained the leader in the cloud computing market, despite stiff competition from Alphabet and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) in recent years. What's more, AI is also helping boost the company's Amazon Web Services revenue. In the third quarter, Amazon's net sales increased by 12% year over year to $201.9 billion.

Story Continues

AWS revenue was $46 billion, up 39% year over year -- the strongest growth rate it has recorded in 18 quarters. Amazon's EPS decreased 3% year over year to $1.89. AWS continues to account for most of Amazon's operating profits, and demand for the company's services remains strong, as evidenced by its $578 billion AWS backlog, which the company said grew in the triple digits year over year.

Amazon could make significant margin gains in the medium term by doubling down on custom AI chips, which tend to be more cost-effective than comparable GPUs ( graphics processing units ). Further, the company's AI initiatives could also improve its e-commerce business, which remains its largest source of sales. Lastly, Amazon's PEG ratio is only about 0.6, which makes the stock look like a steal at current levels. Long-term investors bullish on AI's prospects can hardly go wrong with this stock.

3. Micron Technology

Micron Technology designs memory chips, which are critical components in the AI value chain. In fact, a shortage in this industry has granted the semiconductor leader significant pricing power. Its revenue and earnings have skyrocketed as a result. In the fourth quarter of its fiscal year 2026, which ended on Sept. 3, Micron's revenue grew by 379% year over year to $54.23 billion.

The company's non-GAAP earnings per share were $33.42, up 1,003% compared to the year-ago period.

How long will the memory chip shortage last? Perhaps until 2028 or 2029, according to some projections, potentially providing a strong tailwind to Micron through the medium term. And although the company faces the risk of slowing top- and bottom-line growth -- as well as potential regulatory problems -- the market has already factored these in. Micron's PEG ratio is only 0.2, which makes the stock dirt cheap right now.

news.Title: Missed the Anthropic IPO? These 3 Stocks Give You Immediate Exposure.
news.Content:
Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) is Wall Street's newest public AI stock, and there is a ton of excitement surrounding it. However, not everyone wants to be a Day 1 investor. Stocks frequently behave oddly and erratically over their first few months of trading, and many investors don't want to invest in a company until it has released a few quarterly earnings reports' worth of data about the business.

I fall into that more-cautious category, but there are a few stocks that don't have new-stock risk that are well positioned to benefit from Anthropic going public. Three of those that I'm eyeing are Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

These three benefit in different ways, but I think each of them serves as an excellent alternative to investing in Anthropic right away.

Image source: Getty Images.

Nvidia

Nvidia is well-known in the tech world for having developed the best accelerated computing ecosystem available. It has no rival when it comes to its combination of hardware prowess, controlling software, and other attributes.

Anthropic recognizes this, which is why it has chosen Nvidia to be one of its primary computing unit suppliers. Now that Anthropic has secured more funding for computing resources via its IPO, Nvidia will be a big beneficiary.

Additionally, Nvidia owns Anthropic shares and planned to buy more during the IPO process. If Anthropic thrives, then so will its investment.

Nvidia is currently undergoing some leadership turmoil, and the stock has sold off heavily as a result. This could be an excellent buying opportunity, as the business model is still intact and revenues are growing quickly, as evidenced by its most recent quarterly results.

Nvidia is still a great company and a force to be reckoned with in the AI computing world. As more and more computing power is needed to run a growing number of AI workloads, Nvidia will be one of the primary beneficiaries.

Amazon and Alphabet

Amazon and Alphabet are two of Anthropic's biggest partners. Anthropic doesn't own any of its computing power; it chooses to rent it from cloud computing providers like Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Alphabet's Google Cloud.

From these two, Anthropic selects the best computing unit for the workload, whether it's an Nvidia graphics processing unit (GPU) or one of the custom AI chips available on either of these cloud platforms. Moreover, Amazon and Alphabet have invested heavily in the AI lab; between them, they own nearly 30% of Anthropic.

Story Continues

Between their relationships as compute providers and their massive ownership stakes, both companies have plenty of potential for upside if Anthropic ends up being the AI lab of choice and proves a profitable operation long term.

So, even if you choose not to invest in Anthropic directly, by owning shares of these two, you're indirectly investing in Anthropic. It is a wise move for investors to hold stakes in Amazon, Alphabet, and Nvidia, and to be patient as we wait to see what happens with Anthropic stock.

Indeed, even without the Anthropic connection, these three look pretty attractively valued right now relative to next year's expected earnings.

GOOG PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

With Nvidia trading at a dirt-cheap 9.5 times next year's expected earnings, it's easily the lowest-priced stock of this trio. Alphabet trades at a very reasonable 18.5 times forward earnings, especially considering that the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) trades at 18.8. Amazon is the most expensive at 24.5 times next year's earnings, but I still think that's a fair price tag for a company of its dominance.

These stocks will benefit immensely from Anthropic's IPO. They serve as great alternatives to investing directly in it right now, and investors may be better off buying these three instead of Anthropic, at least until more is known about the business.

news.Title: Anthropic's Record IPO: Can It Lift AI Stocks?
news.Content:
Anthropic has completed the largest IPO in history, raising $81.34 billion and topping the $75 billion SpaceX (SPCX) raised in its base deal in June. The stock priced at $83, above its $70–$78 range, and opened at $111.50, a 34% jump.

With the AI trade under pressure, the question is what this deal says about AI demand, and whether that is enough to lift the rest of the sector.

What the IPO Says About AI Stocks

The numbers behind the IPO may matter more than the IPO itself. Anthropic's sales reached $17 billion in the third quarter, more than 12 times the year-ago level. Its prospectus also lists $518 billion in future cloud, computing and infrastructure bills.

That spending is someone else's revenue and it flows to the companies that rent out the computing power, supply the electricity and manage the servers.

There is a catch though, as a deal this size soaks up a lot of investor cash, and record IPOs have often marked peaks in enthusiasm. The valuation also came in far short of the $2 trillion some on Wall Street had floated before the AI selloffs.

Still, investors paid above the range in a weak tape. Here are three stocks tied to the spending.

Amazon Stock Holding up in Weak Tape

Amazon (AMZN) may be the most direct way to play Anthropic outside of ANT itself. Roughly $110 billion of Anthropic's compute bill goes to Amazon through April 2036 and Amazon also holds a 14.7% stake in the company, worth ~$170 billion.

The stock has held up through the AI selloff. Shares are up 16% this year and 2% over the past four weeks, and trade at 20.8x forward earnings. Amazon carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) after missing estimates by 6% last quarter.

Shares of Amazon have held up quite well in this challenging market environment. Currently the stock sits in a large upward trending channel, and just below its highs.

Image Source: TradingView

Vertiv Shares Boast a Top Zacks Rank

Vertiv (VRT) sells the power and cooling gear that goes inside AI data centers. Third quarter sales climbed 61% to $4.31 billion, and management lifted its 2026 sales outlook to a range of $14.45 billion to $14.85 billion. Orders doubled from a year earlier.

Analysts have followed. Earnings estimates for this year are up 6.9% over the past month, and next year's are up 8.9%, giving Vertiv a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) .

The stock has gone the other way. Shares are down 50% off their highs and trade at 19.9x next year's earnings. That said, the stock looks like it may be finding buyers above the $180 level.

Story Continues

Bloom Energy Stock at a Key Level of Support

Bloom Energy (BE) makes fuel cells that generate electricity onsite, for data centers that cannot wait for a grid connection. Revenue jumped 138% to a record $1.24 billion in the third quarter. The company also lifted its full year revenue forecast to between $4.4 billion and $4.6 billion. Earnings beat estimates by 32%.

This is the high-risk name of the three. The stock is down 51% off its highs, though still up 97% this year, and trades at 51x this year's earnings. Bloom holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) , even with this year's estimates up 23% in a month.

The stock does appear to be holding so far at a key level of support. Investors should keep an eye on the $160 level for a potential tell on the next move.

What is Next for AI Stocks?

Record IPOs have a habit of marking tops in enthusiasm. That signal is harder to read this time. Sentiment on AI stocks is already low, with Vertiv and Bloom both down sharply in recent weeks. It is tough to call a peak in a group that has already sold off.

The better guide may be SpaceX. Shares finished their first day 19% above the $135 offer price. They later ran as high as $225 and ultimately fell as low as $104 and today trade at ~138. That is 36% below the high and only just above the IPO price, five months later.

If that is any indication, Anthropic stock could struggle in the months ahead, even if the business keeps growing. The IPO looks like a good read on AI demand. It is not a reason to chase ANT on day one.

news.Title: Google's AI Space Test Moves Beyond a Single Satellite
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Alphabet's Google (GOOGL) has selected Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to launch a group of AI computing satellites in early 2029. The agreement gives Google's Project Suncatcher its first dedicated heavy-lift mission and moves the company closer to testing whether a network of solar-powered satellites can run workloads that require data centers on Earth.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with META.

Is GOOG fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket is slated to launch in the first quarter of 2029. Google says each satellite will carry its own tensor processing units, or TPUs, with roughly the computing capacity of one data center rack. The satellites will enter a sun-synchronous orbit designed to give them near-continuous access to sunlight. Google's longer-term goal is to link satellites so they can work together on machine learning tasks.

The deal follows a smaller flight. Google and Planet Labs (PL) launched a prototype on a SpaceX rideshare mission on Oct. 1. Later that month, Google said it sent a prompt from the ground to a Gemma 4 model running on the satellite and received a haiku in response. That showed one TPU-equipped satellite could run a model in orbit and return its output to Earth. The new launch is designed to put several satellites in orbit, each with the computing capacity to do more substantial work.

Investors Takeaway

The appeal is access to solar power as terrestrial AI data centers compete for electricity, land and grid connections. The economics depend on how much usable computing capacity Google can get into orbit and keep running. Chips still generate heat in space, where conventional air cooling is unavailable. Engineers also have to account for radiation, which can damage hardware or corrupt data, and make sure links between satellites are fast enough to share workloads.

For Alphabet shareholders, the next milestone is evidence that several satellites can work together reliably and that the cost of launching and operating them can compete with building more capacity on Earth. The companies did not disclose financial terms or announce a commercial service. A credible cost comparison would have to account for replacing failed or outdated equipment, which is much easier to do in a data center on the ground.

For Blue Origin, the agreement adds a dedicated mission for New Glenn. For Google, it provides a way to test orbital computing at a larger scale while its engineers work through the technical hurdles that will determine whether it can become a practical source of capacity.

news.Title: Why Alphabet Stock Popped Today
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) stock jumped 2.2% through 11:45 a.m. ET Thursday on news that the company is partnering with rising space star Blue Origin.

Together, the companies plan to challenge Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) in orbit -- and build a constellation of AI satellites .

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Google + Blue Origin: Better together?

Working through Alphabet's core Google business, Alphabet has signed a launch services agreement for Blue Origin to launch solar-powered AI satellites under what Google calls " Project Suncatcher ."

This project actually began last month with a smallsat express rocket launch from SpaceX. Among other cargo, this rocket carried Google's first Suncatcher prototype satellite to orbit to confirm that Google's artificial intelligence Tensor Processing Units work properly in space. With SpaceX threatening to halt future Falcon 9 commercial launches, however, Google was forced to find itself a new launch partner.

And Blue Origin won that business.

What's next for Google and Blue Origin

Blue Origin's first launch for Project Suncatcher will happen in Q1 2029, and this will be a dedicated heavy-lift launch. That means the entire New Glenn rocket -- all 45 tons of payload capacity of it -- will be crammed full of Google Suncatcher AI satellites.

How many satellites will that work out to, exactly? How much will Google pay Blue Origin for the launch? How many Suncatcher satellites does Google intend to launch in total over time -- and how many rocket launches will that involve?

The companies gave us answers to exactly none of these questions -- which makes it difficult to estimate how much this contract might be worth to Blue Origin over time (or how much it will cost Alphabet, either)! What does seem clear, though, is that -- however much money is involved -- none of it will be going to SpaceX.

news.Title: Anthropic Stock Is Now Trading. Should You Buy ANT Today?
news.Content:
The wait is over.

Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) stock finally made its public debut in the largest IPO in history. The company raised $81.3 billion, topping the $75 billion raised by the previous record holder -- Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX). On a fully diluted basis, the maker of Claude is now valued at just about $1.5 trillion. That makes it, on day one, bigger than Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A) (NYSE: BRK.B) and just behind Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

With all the hoopla, you're probably asking yourself: Should I buy in ? Let's take a look.

Anthropic revenue, losses, and spending commitments

Anthropic creates advanced AI models -- Claude -- and sells access to them. While many people are familiar with using Claude through an app on their phone or desktop -- the massive growth driver has been enterprise clients who largely access Claude through an API -- basically, [what is api].

The sales growth has been mind-boggling: revenue was $386 million in 2024, $4.6 billion in 2025, and $33.2 billion in just the first nine months of 2026.

But of course, that revenue isn't free. Frontier AI is expensive. Anthropic lost $104 billion on that $33.2 billion in sales. Most of it, $94.3 billion, is an accounting charge on its convertible notes, but even setting that aside, the company still lost about $1.3 billion at the operating level.

And then there is the future spending: Anthropic has about $895 billion in purchase commitments -- roughly half of which is set to be spent before 2030 -- mostly for the chips and data centers that power Claude.

Anthropic stock valuation compared with Nvidia

At $1.5 trillion, Anthropic is valued at roughly 28 times its expected 2026 revenue of $53 billion. Compare that to Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) -- no one's idea of a cheap stock, and a company raking in cash -- which goes for about 10 times sales. The assumption, of course, is that the current pace of sales growth will continue and that the multiple will compress. I'm not convinced. We already saw a slowdown in the rate of top-line growth from Q2 to Q3.

I also think profitability is going to continue to be elusive as the company's costs continue to climb. Remember, Nvidia's substantially smaller price-to-sales is for a company that pulls in $226 billion in net earnings a year.

Story Continues

Dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

Anthropic stock is priced with an extremely rosy view of the future, and, in my humble opinion, it's driven by hype -- and hype fades. I wouldn't buy the stock unless the valuation comes back to earth.

Why to wait on Anthropic stock, even if you're bullish

Even if you're sold on the company long term and its rich valuation doesn't faze you, there's still plenty of reason to wait. IPOs, especially mega IPOs like this, are highly volatile, and first-day investors often get hit. Meta Platforms, for instance, dropped more than 30% in year one, and SpaceX, which opened at $150 a share in June, is currently below that.

Regardless of your view on the business, I would wait for the IPO dust to settle before considering jumping in.

news.Title: Can MRVL's Custom Silicon Business Drive Its Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL is expanding its presence in the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market through its custom silicon business. The company develops custom compute and connectivity solutions for hyperscalers seeking to build and optimize AI infrastructure. Its portfolio includes custom XPUs and XPU-attach products, which help address growing requirements for AI computing, memory and data movement.

MRVL's custom silicon opportunity is gaining traction as hyperscalers expand their investments in AI infrastructure. The company expects demand for its XPU and XPU-attach solutions to accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2027. Management remains confident that custom silicon revenues will more than double year over year in fiscal 2028, with further acceleration expected in fiscal 2029. This provides greater visibility into the business' contribution to MRVL's multi-year growth outlook.

An expanded commercial agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscaler further strengthens this opportunity. The agreement covers existing programs, new design wins and potential future projects. Its scope extends beyond AI inference accelerators to include storage controllers, network interface controllers (NICs), memory interface controllers and near-memory compute solutions associated with the customer's tensor processing unit ecosystem. The broader engagement creates opportunities for MRVL to supply multiple components across AI computing and connectivity architectures.

The company is also benefiting from its expanding relationships across the AI ecosystem. Its strategic partnership with NVIDIA and investments in networking technologies complement its custom silicon portfolio. By combining custom compute solutions with high-speed connectivity, switching and optical interconnect technologies, MRVL is positioning itself to address multiple requirements of increasingly complex AI infrastructure. This broader portfolio could strengthen its competitive position as hyperscalers develop next-generation AI systems.

However, the expansion carries execution and profitability risks. Custom silicon programs typically depend on customer design decisions, deployment schedules and production ramps. Moreover, management expects the accelerating custom product mix to weigh on near-term gross margins. MRVL's increasing dependence on large hyperscalers also raises customer concentration risks. Nevertheless, sustained design wins and the expected revenue acceleration position custom silicon as an important driver of its growth through fiscal 2028 and beyond.

Story Continues

How Competitors Fare Against MRVL

MRVL faces stiff competition from Broadcom AVGO and Advanced Micro Devices AMD. Broadcom is a leader in the domain of custom silicon solutions for data centers. Broadcom's advanced 3.5D XDSiP packaging platform is critical to ensure the performance and efficiency of custom AI XPUs.

Broadcom's relationships with leading hyperscale and frontier AI customers give it direct insight into workload requirements and help shape differentiated accelerators. The company continues to work with six core XPU customers across multiyear programs. Advanced Micro Devices is another established player in the custom silicon solutions and AI accelerator market. Advanced Micro Devices offers semi-custom SoCs and Instinct Accelerators to power data centers. AMD is broadening its data center AI opportunity from Instinct accelerators to the Helios rack-scale platform.

MRVL's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Marvell Technology have gained 71.3% year to date compared with the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's growth of 3.5%.
