news.Title: The Deal Behind Needham’s Call on Lumentum (LITE)
news.Content:
We just published a list of the Forget Nvidia: 10 Stocks Wall Street is Betting on Right Now and Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) ranked 6th on this list.

Stocks ended a jumpy week with gains on paper and a sour finish. Reuters reported on November 13 that the S&P 500 fell 0.40% and the Nasdaq fell 0.91% on the day, yet the S&P 500 still rose 2.51% for the week, ending four straight weekly declines. The rebound did not survive the final session, and the reason sat in the bond market rather than in earnings.

Photo by osamu nakazawa on Unsplash

Hot Inflation Forces a Rethink on Rates

Consumer price data released on November 10 showed headline inflation rising 0.4% in October, above forecasts, with the core measure also coming in hotter than expected. Two-year Treasury yields jumped about 19 basis points that day, the biggest one-day move since April 2025, as traders abandoned hopes of a pause.

Policymakers have since leaned toward tightening. One Federal Reserve governor has argued for a December increase, possibly of half a point, and a regional Fed president wants at least two more increases of 25 basis points from a policy rate of 3.75% to 4.00%. Yahoo Finance reported that the 10-year yield stayed above 5% after leaping more than 13 basis points on November 12, and that traders now treat a December hike as a certainty.

The pressure has reached households. Freddie Mac put the average 30-year mortgage rate at 7.11% for the week ended November 12. Investors asking which beaten-down names might still be worth owning can browse 10 Oversold AI Stocks: Where Wall Street Analysts Are Spotting 50%+ Upside .

Chip Stocks Take the Brunt

Semiconductors absorbed the worst of it. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 3.4% on November 13, and technology was the weakest of the 11 S&P 500 sectors with a 1.7% decline. The VIX volatility gauge moved back above 20. A separate Yahoo Finance staff report said chip stocks had shed more than $650 billion in two days as the 10-year yield climbed about 30 basis points in a week to roughly 5.15%, its biggest weekly rise since April 2025.

Other data pointed the same way. The dollar reached a 19-month high, and Reuters reported that October producer prices were up 6.5% from a year earlier, while the two-year yield finished the week near 4.87%, its largest weekly increase in more than two years.

For anyone who wants a longer view of the sector, 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade looks past the current swings. The Fed meets on December 9, and the inflation and jobs reports that arrive before then are likely to move stocks more than any single earnings release.

Story Continues

Lumentum made it to our list because it has an average upside potential of 77.0%. Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) in an all-stock deal announced on November 2, the same day Lumentum reported its fiscal first quarter of 2027. Holders will receive Marvell shares rather than cash.

Revenue was $1.26 billion, more than double the year before, and non-GAAP earnings were $4.57 per share. The company guided fiscal second-quarter revenue to $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion. CEO Michael Hurlston said that "our OCS demand visibility has expanded significantly in recent months," and that the company had won a second major deal for optics built alongside processors. Management also said its cloud module business continues to show strength. Lumentum makes lasers and optical components that move data inside AI data centers.

Needham analyst Alex Henderson cut his price target to $800 from $1,040 on November 3 and kept a Buy rating. The deal is the other debate. Holders have to decide whether the all-stock terms are fair, and the value they receive moves with Marvell's shares. Our earlier look at the company's demand and valuation is in Lumentum (LITE) Can't Meet Demand. Can Its Valuation Hold Up? .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of LITE as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: What Marvell’s (MRVL) Lumentum Deal Adds to Its Anthropic Growth Story
news.Content:
Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) ranks sixth on our list of 10 Best Stocks to Buy Ahead of Anthropic's IPO .

The company behind Claude has launched its roadshow for a proposed offering of 825 million shares at $70 to $78 apiece and has applied to trade on Nasdaq under ANT. For public-market investors, the attention extends beyond the debut itself. Anthropic's suppliers already trade on stock exchanges, and their businesses offer several ways to follow the spending behind its expansion.

The question is how much of that opportunity will reach shareholders after the equipment, construction, and financing bills are paid.

There is considerable demand for the offering, but confidence in the business is less uniform. Reuters reported that orders reached roughly six times the available shares during the roadshow, even as investors questioned whether Anthropic could preserve its lead and expand Claude's appeal beyond coding. Those concerns matter to suppliers as well.

A successful fundraising would strengthen a major customer's finances; it would not settle the debate over how much companies will eventually pay for AI or how quickly the industry can earn back its infrastructure spending.

Amazon's Infrastructure Creates an Indirect Opportunity

Marvell sits behind part of the computing infrastructure Anthropic is securing from Amazon. Its custom chips and networking products connect the AI spending story to equipment orders. That makes it an indirect supplier play, with the opportunity tied to the buildout of Amazon's chip ecosystem rather than ownership of Anthropic shares.

The median analyst target of $300 implies 91.38% upside.

Data Center Demand Supports Growth

The latest reported quarter produced $2.739 billion in revenue, up 37% year over year, while data-center revenue grew 46%. Marvell subsequently reaffirmed a $3.15 billion revenue midpoint for the following quarter and narrowed the expected range. Those figures suggest demand is already supporting the business. The longer-term question is how much additional growth comes from custom processors and the faster connections needed as computing clusters become larger and more complex.

Lumentum Deal Brings Expansion and Execution Risks

The proposed Lumentum acquisition adds another layer. Marvell agreed to an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion, combining its semiconductor capabilities with Lumentum's optical technologies. The agreement remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. Our coverage of the deal behind TD Cowen's Marvell downgrade captures the disagreement around that expansion.

Story Continues

A broader product offering could help, but integration, dilution and execution make the outcome more complicated than simply adding two growing suppliers together.

Insider Monkey's Q2 2026 database shows 96 hedge fund holders, reflecting meaningful institutional participation. The target leaves room for a recovery in confidence, although the acquisition creates questions that an Anthropic IPO cannot settle. Investors have to judge whether demand for custom chips and optical networking can keep supporting earnings while management prepares a much larger business for its next stage of growth.

news.Title: Applied Materials vs. Marvell Technology: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As the race for dominance in artificial intelligence intensifies, choosing the right infrastructure provider is critical. Should you invest in equipment giant Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) or connectivity specialist Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL)?

Applied Materials supplies the tools that actually build the chips, making it a foundational player in the semiconductor ecosystem. Marvell designs the custom chips and networking components that move data between servers. Comparing these two reveals different ways to play the ongoing shift toward high-performance computing and massive data center expansion.

The case for Applied Materials

Applied Materials sells materials engineering solutions used to produce nearly every new chip and advanced display in the world. It serves a concentrated customer base of logic, foundry, and memory manufacturers, including giants like Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU). Two specific customers accounted for approximately 19% and 15% of net revenue, respectively. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 25, 2026, revenue reached nearly $34.4 billion. This represented growth of roughly 21.4% compared to the prior period, driven by strong demand for advanced chipmaking equipment. Net income totaled approximately $10.1 billion, showcasing the profitability possible at this scale.

As of Applied Materials' October 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3. This ratio measures total debt against shareholder equity, with lower numbers typically suggesting less financial leverage. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, is roughly 2.3. For those following semiconductor stocks , strong cash flow is vital for R&D. In the fiscal year ended Oct. 25, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $6.2 billion.

The case for Marvell Technology

Marvell Technology operates as a fabless supplier, meaning it designs high-end semiconductor solutions but outsources the actual manufacturing. The company focuses on data center core networks and the network edge, serving original equipment manufacturers and cloud service providers. For its most recent annual reporting period, two customers each accounted for 10% or more of net revenue, and the 10 largest customers collectively accounted for 82% of net revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached nearly $9.5 billion. This figure reflects growth of close to 30.6% over the previous 12 months as the company expanded its footprint in AI infrastructure. Net income for the same period was approximately $2.6 billion, marking a significant turnaround from previous years.

Story Continues

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.3. Its current ratio is approximately 2, indicating a solid ability to meet short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was close to $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 33.8% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Applied Materials faces significant geographic concentration, with a heavy reliance on customers in China. This exposure makes the company sensitive to trade policies and export restrictions. It also manages legal risks involving export controls, including a $252 million settlement reached in February 2026 for export violations involving Semiconductor Manufacturing International. Furthermore, its reliance on complex global supply chains creates vulnerability to regional disruptions or inventory obsolescence.

Marvell Technology has high customer concentration. Its 10 largest clients account for nearly 82% of revenue, and it often competes with rivals like Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO). The company is also navigating a massive $115 billion pending acquisition of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE). This deal introduces risks related to shareholder dilution and the complex process of integrating two large organizations. Additionally, Marvell's dependency on third-party foundries in the Pacific Rim creates supply chain risks if regional political conflicts arise.

Valuation comparison

Applied Materials currently appears to be the more conservative value choice, while Marvell Technology commands a higher premium given its faster growth profile.

The forward P/E compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, helping you see how much you are paying for every dollar of projected profit. The P/S ratio measures the market price relative to sales over the past 12 months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Marvell and Applied Materials are riding the current tech boom, with both stocks hitting all-time highs earlier this year. They've since pulled back a considerable amount, but they're still handily outpacing the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) by massive margins:

AMAT data by YCharts

There's not a ton of daylight between the two stocks' recent returns. And as for business performance, Applied Materials has a slightly higher net margin, while Marvell is posting stronger revenue growth.

I lean toward Applied Materials in this matchup. Marvell's revenue growth is impressive, but its pending acquisition of Lumentum introduces a fair amount of risk. There's the possibility of dilution, but there's also the potential that the combined company doesn't create the cost-savings and synergies management had hoped for. That could lead to significant writedowns, which would almost certainly impact the stock negatively.

Applied Materials just seems to have less risk, which makes it my pick for 2027 and beyond.

news.Title: Down 36% in a month at 48x P/E: Is Marvell a dip or a trap?
news.Content:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Investing.com — Intel's weak forecast set off a broad chip sell-off, and November's data-center permitting panic has kept AI hardware under pressure. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) has slid 27.1% over the past month. Yet Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL)—the custom silicon and networking specialist wiring together some of the largest AI server clusters—has plunged 36.2% over the past month to $145.36, less than half its 52-week high of $329.73.

Marvell's slide appears less like a growth scare than a dilution story. Management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to about $12 billion, and analysts forecast 47.0% revenue growth and 42.7% EPS growth this fiscal year, yet the $115 billion all-stock bid for Lumentum would hand Lumentum holders about 33% of the combined company. At 48.3 times trailing earnings, the stock still prices that growth at a premium—before a single new share has been issued.

Catching when a near-50x multiple and lumpy custom chip orders leave a stock exposed to a 36% drawdown is what ProPicks AI is built for. The Custom Silicon Franchise Google Is Paying For

Marvell makes its money designing the custom AI accelerators, optical DSPs, and switching chips that hyperscalers use to tie their data centers together, and that design work creates high switching costs once a chip is in production. In August, Google signed a commercial agreement covering up to $120 billion in sales through fiscal 2033, along with the right to buy a $12.2 billion stake. Management expects the largest revenue impact in fiscal 2029 and beyond.

Second-quarter fiscal 2027 results confirmed that AI demand is still accelerating. Revenue climbed 37% year-over-year and 13% sequentially to a record $2.74 billion, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 edged past the $0.93 estimate. Data center revenue surged 46% to $2.17 billion—79% of total sales—and management guided third-quarter revenue to $3.15 billion. It then lifted its fiscal 2028 outlook to about $18 billion from $16.5 billion, with data center revenue now expected to grow about 60% in fiscal 2027 and more than 60% in fiscal 2028.

Story Continues

Fair Value Tempts Dip-Buyers, but the Risks Stack Up

Wall Street remains largely bullish, but the Lumentum deal split the room. StoneX, UBS and Raymond James held Buy-or-better ratings with targets of $295 to $375. TD Cowen downgraded the stock to Hold and cut its target to $175 from $350, citing equity dilution and deal execution risk. The median analyst price target stands at $310.32, with targets ranging from $175 to $450.

The earnings trend still favors the bulls, with 27 upward EPS revisions against one downward over the past 90 days. InvestingPro's Fair Value models also flag Marvell as undervalued, placing intrinsic value at $180.10 per share—23.9% above the current price and an upside that will tempt dip-buyers.

The main risk is that dip-buyers are taking on several bets at once. The Lumentum deal needs stockholder and regulatory approval before a targeted close in the first half of 2028. Custom silicon ramps have pushed non-GAAP gross margin guidance down to 57.5% to 58.5%, a range management expects to persist into fiscal 2028, while the top 10 customers account for about 82% of revenue and a single distributor for about 37%. Communications and other revenue slipped 3% sequentially to $568 million, with a further low-to-mid-teens decline guided for the third quarter.

Before buying a 36% chip rout, investors must weigh Marvell's custom silicon franchise against Lumentum dilution and margin pressure. A Real Franchise at a Demanding Price

Hyperscalers want Marvell's custom silicon badly enough to sign multi-year commitments. What investors cannot yet price is how much of the growth from those commitments each share will keep once the Lumentum deal closes and custom chip ramps stop weighing on gross margins.

news.Title: 才剛填息！輝達概念股華邦電突翻臉 重挫逾4%
news.Content:
輝達供應鏈的記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）今（18）日除息交易，每股配息2元，參考價108.5元，早盤一度衝上115元順利填息，但受亞洲科技股走弱與新台幣續貶拖累，盤中翻黑下探104.5元、跌幅逾4%。分析師表示，儘管短線賣壓沉重，基本面依舊亮眼。但現在正在跌、籌碼還很亂，千萬別急著現在衝進去接刀。

華邦電今日進行除息交易，每股配發現金股利2元，除息參考價為108.5元；若以昨日收盤價110.5元計算，現金殖利率約1.81%。

華邦電今日股價開高走低，早盤一度衝高至115元、順利完成填息，但受亞洲科技股走弱及新台幣續貶拖累，盤中由紅翻黑，最低下探104.5元，跌幅逾4%。

倫元投顧分析師王春盛指出，儘管市場對記憶體景氣仍抱持期待，但受大盤氛圍與匯率貶值影響，短線賣壓沉重。回歸基本面，華邦電第三季營收達823.31億元，季增37.6%，毛利率高達70.6%，單季EPS為7.58元，累計前三季EPS達15.32元，獲利表現亮眼。操作策略上，王春盛建議持股者可先觀察除息後股價能否止穩並重啟填息走勢；空手者則不宜急於追價，宜等待量縮止穩、外資買盤回籠後再分批布局，並嚴設停損。

華邦電日前召開法說會，總經理陳沛銘指出，市場普遍預期2027年記憶體缺貨狀況恐比今年更嚴重，且下半年緊縮力道將強於上半年。

陳沛銘指出，當前產業景氣呈現嚴重的「AI強、非AI弱」分化現象，第四季消費性需求已出現修正，甚至有客戶直言PC做三季累了，「第四季要休息」，但預期公司第四季營運雖能保持成長，但增長力道將不如前幾季強勁。

news.Title: Nvidia earnings spark premarket rally in chipmakers, neocloud stocks
news.Content:
Investing.com-- Shares of chipmakers and cloud computing firms rose sharply in premarket trading on Wednesday after blowout quarterly earnings from sector giant Nvidia helped restore faith in the artificial intelligence trade.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

By 04:10 ET (09:10 GMT), Nvidia rose 2.9%, while rival AMD rose 2.6%. Intel added 1.6%, Arm jumped 3.4%, Broadcom rose 2.1%, and Super Micro added 4.2%. Marvell, Micron, and U.S.-listed shares of SK Hynix gained more than 3% each.

Among cloud computing stocks, Oracle added 2.5%, while neoclouds Coreweave and Nebius added 5.9% and 7.8%, respectively.

European semiconductor stocks followed suit, rallying after the market open on Wednesday. Siltronic surged nearly 8%, Technoprobe rose 4.3%, while BE Semiconductor, ASML, ASM International, Aixtron and Soitec rose around 3% each. Infineon and STMicroelectronics gained about 2%.

Nvidia posted stronger-than-expected earnings for its third fiscal quarter, and flagged continued, growing demand for its advanced processors from the AI industry.

The print came amid troubled times for the chipmaker, which recently ousted CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang following revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

Huang's exit fueled concerns over more regulatory scrutiny towards Nvidia, while investors also questioned whether new management would continue the chipmaker's massive investments in some of its largest cloud customers, which made it a de-facto central bank for AI infrastructure financing.

But Tuesday's strong earnings helped reinforce the notion that Nvidia's core business remained solid despite the governance scandal. CFO and now interim CEO Colette Kress also reiterated that the company will continue to invest in some of its customers, albeit with more "discipline" in how it commits capital going forward.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

Kress said AI-fueled demand for Nvidia's chips remained robust and was likely to stay strong in the coming quarters. She forecast stronger-than-expected revenue in the current quarter, and said gross margins were set to improve in the coming year.

Story Continues

JPMorgan called the results a "positive datapoint" but said they were not a "clearing event" for concerns about the data center market.

Separately, Citi analysts said the print "reinforced our core investment thesis that demand remains very strong, supply constraints are easing, and interim management is confident enough to raise long-term growth expectations."

Nvidia and broader tech stocks were nursing deep losses heading into Tuesday's print, amid growing uncertainty over what Huang's ouster may imply for the broader AI trade.

Nvidia had slumped nearly 25% so far in November, while the SOX was nursing a near 10% decline.

While Tuesday's print helped spur some buying, Nvidia still traded well below record highs hit earlier in 2026.

The stock still faces overhangs, with U.S. lawmakers increasingly scrutinizing the firm over potential chip sales to Chinese entities.

Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter have agreed to testify before Congress on the matter.

But separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission had opened a probe into Nvidia.

Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.

news.Title: Credo, Marvell settle intellectual property battle over data center cable tech
news.Content:

The agreement clears a legal overhang in the rapidly expanding market for artificial intelligence data infrastructure, where both firms compete to supply critical hardware components.

While financial and licensing terms remain confidential, the accord brings a close to contentious intellectual property proceedings that had threatened to complicate commercial deployments.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

The resolution specifically addresses challenges Marvell initiated against Credo's patents before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office in August 2025. For Credo, which specializes in high-speed copper and optical interconnect solutions designed to link chips and clusters within AI data centers, the settlement removes a direct threat to its core intellectual property portfolio. Investors responded positively to the reduced legal uncertainty, lifting both stocks as the companies put the regulatory battle behind them.

news.Title: ‘How Could You Not?’ Says Investor About Sandisk Stock
news.Content:
Sandisk ( NASDAQ:SNDK ) is selling flash memory to AI data centers about as fast as it can make it, but that has done little for investors' morale recently. The stock keeps falling anyway, with shares drifting lower since their late-June peak.

The past couple of weeks have made things worse. AI stocks dropped after the Democrats' midterm sweep raised fears that tighter rules could slow data center construction, and then fell again when Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO on Nov. 12. Monday was the third losing day in a row, and traders are now waiting for Nvidia's quarterly report after the bell today.

The stock currently sits about 65% below its June record. That's just days before Sandisk's 8-for-1 stock split takes effect on Nov. 20.

Promotion

BLACK FRIDAY SALE

Get 75% Off TipRanks Premium and unlock powerful investing tools to make smarter, more confident investment decisions

Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Learn more about TipRanks Premium

The problem, says investor Infinity Curve (IC), has less to do with the company and more to do with the market still treating Sandisk like the old boom-and-bust memory maker and missing how much the business has changed. In fiscal Q1 2027, revenue jumped 378% year over year to $11 billion, and non-GAAP gross margin came in at 85.1%. Management expects $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion in revenue this quarter.

IC accepts that margins like that won't last forever. Still, management said about 60% of the sequential sales jump came from higher volume rather than higher prices. The investor sees that as a sign of real demand. Data centers drive most of it. That segment's revenue rose 61% from the prior quarter to $4.8 billion, and exabytes shipped grew about 330% YoY.

IC argues that AI inference needs more storage than DRAM or HBM can supply at a sensible cost. Larger context windows and more complex agentic tools are two reasons. IC gives little weight to Sandisk's high-bandwidth flash plans and bases the thesis on products already on the market.

The investor's biggest reason for optimism is the contract book. Sandisk has $88.9 billion in remaining performance obligations (RPOs), mostly from multiyear supply deals that cover about half of fiscal 2027 bits and two-thirds of fiscal 2028 bits. About 95% of those customers are investment grade, and many have put up collateral. IC is careful here. The deals don't fix margins and only partly protect Sandisk, so the cycle hasn't gone away. Even so, keeping a bit more profit in a downturn could justify a much higher valuation.

Story Continues

The cash keeps coming in, too. Sandisk generated about $5.7 billion of adjusted free cash flow last quarter. IC's only complaint is that $5 billion of it went to buybacks at today's prices, and the investor would have liked to see more kept back for a rainy day. A roughly 40% jump in receivables from the prior quarter is also on IC's radar, though as something to keep an eye on rather than a red flag.

At about 6.5x trailing earnings, the stock already looks cheap, but IC doesn't lean on that number, since it could reflect peak profits. Even if gross margin falls to 72% on $42 billion of yearly revenue, which would still be very high for a memory maker, IC finds the shares have plenty of room to run.

None of this means the NAND cycle has gone away. NAND prices could fall if Samsung, SK hynix or Micron ramp up production, and that would hit the sales not covered by contracts. Outside data centers, things are already softer, with consumer revenue down 29% from the prior quarter. Sandisk also relies on its Kioxia venture for almost all of its wafers, and on a fairly small group of large customers.

Still, IC believes the contracts should help Sandisk hold on to more of its earnings when the next downturn comes.

Bottom line, Infinity Curve rates SNDK a Strong Buy. (To watch Infinity Curve's track record, click here )

So does the analyst consensus, a rating based on 11 Buys and 3 Holds. At $2,131, the average price target implies shares will gain 163% over the coming months. ( See SNDK stock forecast )

news.Title: 4 Dates That Could Move the Stock Market in Epic Fashion This Week. Here's What Investors Need to Know.
news.Content:
Wall Street is heading into one of the most consequential trading weeks of 2026, with several major events capable of influencing investor sentiment converging at once. Between Nov. 17 and Nov. 20, investors will receive Nvidia 's (NASDAQ:NVDA) fiscal third-quarter earnings report, the Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes, and the initial public offering (IPO) of artificial intelligence (AI) developer Anthropic. Meanwhile, memory manufacturer Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) is preparing to execute an 8-for-1 stock split that could attract attention from retail investors.

These events arrive during a particularly uncertain period for the stock market. Concerns around AI valuations, interest rate policy, political uncertainty, and corporate leadership shakeups have introduced unusual levels of volatility into an otherwise multiyear bull market.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Let's take a look at five important events taking place this week and what investors should be watching.

Image source: Getty Images.

Nov. 17: Nvidia's earnings will be about more than financials

Nvidia is scheduled to report earnings after the market closes on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The company guided for revenue of $108 billion, representing roughly 89% growth year over year.

Ordinarily, investors would be focusing on whether Nvidia exceeds this forecast and provides encouraging guidance for the upcoming quarter. However, this earnings announcement comes under much different circumstances following Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation as CEO. As a result, another quarter of robust financial growth will likely take a back seat to questions surrounding Nvidia's leadership transition.

Huang played an instrumental role in transforming Nvidia into the dominant supplier of AI accelerators, making his departure a meaningful source of uncertainty for investors. During the earnings call, my hunch is that analysts will be trying to get some clarity around the company's succession plans and its ability to maintain competitive advantages without its former leader.

Nov. 18 and 19: Anthropic's IPO and the Federal Reserve collide

Anthropic is expected to finalize the pricing of its IPO on Nov. 18. The start-up behind the Claude chatbot is indicating an offering price in the range of $70 to $78, potentially raising around $64 billion at the upper end. Such a debut would rank among the largest IPOs in stock market history , making it an important test of demand for AI investments.

Story Continues

Anthropic is subsequently expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Thursday, Nov. 19. The offering could generate widespread enthusiasm throughout the AI ecosystem, particularly among companies with financial and commercial relationships with the developer. Amazon , Alphabet , and Space Exploration Technologies are among the companies investors could scrutinize as Anthropic's valuation and infrastructure spending commitments receive greater attention.

Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve is scheduled to release minutes from its October monetary policy meeting at 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 18. Smart investors will look for clues about whether the Fed is considering another interest rate hike before the end of the year. Any indication that interest rates could remain elevated might pressure growth stocks, whose valuations are highly sensitive to changes in borrowing costs.

Nov. 20: Sandisk's stock split could be another catalyst for AI stocks

The week's final major event involves Sandisk, which is preparing to execute an 8-for-1 stock split. The transaction follows a period of extreme volatility for the NAND flash specialist, whose stock has attracted meaningful attention amid surging demand for memory and storage solutions.

Although stock splits do not change a company's underlying valuation, they can still influence investor psychology and trading activity. By reducing the price of individual shares in terms of absolute dollars, Sandisk is making shares more accessible to investors who prefer purchasing whole shares rather than fractional shares.

Prepare for volatility in either direction this week

Ultimately, the combination of Nvidia's earnings, Anthropic's IPO, the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes, and Sandisk's stock split makes this an unusually eventful week for Wall Street. Investors should pay attention to any comments around Nvidia's leadership outlook, Anthropic's reception among institutional investors, and any changes in the Fed's assessment of inflation and interest rates. While these developments will likely fuel short-term volatility, their longer-term implications will depend on how they affect earnings and confidence in the broader economy.

news.Title: Microchip’s Earnings Rebound Meets a Softer Outlook
news.Content:
We just published our list of the 10 Highest Short Interest Large-Cap Tech Stocks Right Now , and Microchip Technology Incorporated ranked 8th on the list.

Technology stocks are facing a new test of investor conviction as hedge funds pull back from the artificial intelligence trade. Bloomberg reported on November 9 that hedge funds sold global technology stocks at one of the fastest weekly rates on record, citing Goldman Sachs prime brokerage data through November 6. Technology was the most heavily net-sold sector globally and in the US, with the percentage rate of selling roughly matching the benchmark set in Goldman's records dating back to 2016. The slump also resulted in the largest wave of single-stock net selling in four months.

The catalyst was not just another debate about overpriced stocks. According to Bloomberg, concerns about political opposition disrupting data-center buildout sparked an aggressive reconsideration of the AI trade. This raises questions about how quickly infrastructure projects can move forward and whether spending commitments would result in profitable growth. Insider Monkey's discussion of the fastest-growing AI stocks to buy highlights a related tension: strong demand and rapid revenue growth can coexist with pressure on share prices when investors question how the expansion will be financed.

The scale of that investment explains why the stakes are so high. According to Insider Monkey's analysis of the cheapest AI data center stocks to buy according to billionaires , the International Energy Agency estimates that hyperscalers would invest over $700 billion in new data centers in 2026. The same article cites CBRE research suggesting that supply in primary North American markets climbed 33.7% year-over-year to 10,903 megawatts in the first half of 2026, while vacancies declined to 1.4%.

The mechanics of short selling help explain what's at stake. A short sale generally involves selling securities that an investor doesn't own or has borrowed for delivery. The seller can profit by buying back the shares at a discount, but will lose money if the price rises. That said, heavily shorted stocks can react strongly when expectations improve. Short sellers may buy stocks to close off losing positions, potentially adding to an advance. The broader market's rebound shows how rapidly sentiment can shift: on November 9, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbed 6.9%, its strongest session since July 30, as investors processed reports of near-record hedge-fund selling of technology stocks. Insider Monkey's coverage of AI stocks dominating the list of biggest winners subsequently reported that Nebius Group gained 15.44% on November 11, compared with the Nasdaq's 1.6% advance.

Story Continues

For investors considering bearish positions, the question is not whether AI demand will increase, but whether the companies that serve it can overcome infrastructure bottlenecks and turn that demand into profitable cash flow.

Microchip made the list on account of its market value of $33.57 billion and a short interest rate of 6.85%. Its 42.27% analyst upside indicates significant potential, while the short position presumably reflects concerns about whether the company's sharp earnings recovery can be sustained in a cyclical semiconductor market.

Microchip Technology Incorporated delivers semiconductors to a variety of areas, including industrial equipment and automotive applications. Its fiscal second-quarter 2027 results showed a significant turnaround, with revenue increasing 42.2% year-over-year and 9.2% sequentially to $1.622 billion, exceeding the midpoint of management's previous projection of $1.604 billion. GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders rose to $373.6 million, or $0.68 per diluted share, from $13.9 million, or $0.03 per share, the year before.

However, the December quarter outlook indicated a more measured near-term trend. Management expects revenue of $1.573 billion to $1.638 billion, a sequential decrease of 3% to 1%, and non-GAAP earnings of $0.87 to $0.95 per share. It also projected an adjusted gross margin of 64%-65% and an adjusted operating margin of 37%-38.5%, both lower than the September quarter's figures of 66.5% and 39.5%.

The company's balance sheet and valuation add another layer to the argument. The major concern is whether the earnings recovery can strengthen the balance sheet while still supporting shareholder payouts, a trade-off that Insider Monkey analyzed in its comparison of Microchip and competitor Lattice Semiconductor .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MCHP as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Marvell Just Made a Massive Move Against Broadcom. How to Play MRVL Stock Now.
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) has decided that winning the AI infrastructure race takes more than designing faster chips. Its $115 billion agreement to acquire Lumentum (LITE) is a bid to control more of the connections that make enormous AI systems work. This move brings Broadcom (AVGO) into the picture and increases the risks for Marvell's shareholders. Here's how it could play out.

MRVL stock is up 71% so far this year, beating the S&P 500 Index ($SPX), whereas AVGO stock is down about 3%.

More News from Barchart

Jensen Huang Said 'Nothing Would Give Me More Joy' Than Paying Higher Taxes and Called Owing $8 Billion a 'Privilege'

Dear MicroStrategy Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 30

Walmart Gets $2.9 Billion in Tariff Refunds, Ford $1.3 Billion, and Apple $2.2 Billion: The Average Household Paid an Estimated $700 and Got Nothing

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Marvell Wants a Bigger Place in the AI Stack

Marvell's $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum aims to unite two vital pillars of AI infrastructure into a single powerhouse. This all-stock deal merges Marvell's custom AI accelerators, cutting-edge interconnects, networking switches, and semiconductor expertise with Lumentum's high-performance lasers, advanced optical transceivers, and optical circuit switching. Lumentum additionally contributes its specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing, including indium phosphide technology, a key ingredient for next-generation optical components.

After the deal closes, current Marvell investors will likely own about two-thirds of the new company, while Lumentum investors own the rest. Because the deal uses a fixed share-exchange ratio, changes in Marvell's stock price before the deal closes will affect how much Lumentum shareholders receive. Both groups of shareholders face market swings during the long approval process. The risk impacts everyone.

Marvell expects this merger will create a broader connectivity portfolio, covering everything from links between data centers and servers to connections between processors within advanced AI systems. With this bold move, the company believes the combined business could tap into a $550 billion market opportunity, generating over $1 billion in annual cost synergies and boosting long-term revenue and margins. Marvell forecasts that the acquisition will begin adding to its adjusted EPS in the first year after completion. The companies are targeting a closing in early 2028, subject to regulatory clearance and shareholder approval.

Story Continues

So how does Broadcom fit into this? Broadcom stands out as a strong rival, powering hyperscalers' vast data centers with its custom AI accelerators and networking silicon. Marvell operates in overlapping markets, including custom silicon, switching, and connectivity. The main idea is to move data, not just process it. AI accelerators need fast connections to communicate with each other, as well as with storage and networking gear. Copper is still useful, but as systems scale, distance, bandwidth, and power become bigger issues. Optical technology can send data farther and faster, and often does so more efficiently. Marvell already offers optical digital signal processors, interconnects, and switches. Lumentum adds advanced lasers, optical transceivers, switching technology, and specialized semiconductor manufacturing. According to Reuters , Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum signals its intent to challenge Broadcom more aggressively for a share of AI investment.

This is Why Marvell Wants to Move Faster

Marvell's fiscal 2027 second-quarter earnings show why Marvell wants to move faster. Revenue surged to $2.74 billion, a 37% year-over-year (YoY) leap and a 13% jump from the previous quarter. Data center sales soared to $2.17 billion, accounting for 79% of total revenue and up 46% from last year. The real powerhouse behind this momentum is the explosive demand for AI.

Looking ahead, Marvell projects Q3 revenue to hit $3.15 billion at the midpoint, denoting a 15% jump from last quarter and over 50% YoY growth. The company has also boosted its fiscal 2027 revenue target to about $12 billion, up from $11.5 billion, and raised its fiscal 2028 outlook to around $18 billion, up from $16.5 billion, aiming for roughly 50% growth.

Marvell's Q2 adjusted gross margin stood at 58.9%, while adjusted earnings per share climbed 40% YoY to $0.94. CFO Dan Durn said adjusted operating margin was expected to enter the company's 38% to 40% long-term target range as fiscal 2027 progressed.

Management pointed to surging demand across interconnect, switching, and custom silicon. Marvell reported strong demand for its 800-gigabit optical products, while its 1.6-terabit business is gaining momentum. The company expects its 51.2-terabit switching products to more than double this fiscal year. By fiscal 2028, management anticipates data center revenue to soar over 60%, with custom silicon revenue more than doubling. Marvell is also in talks with major customers about scale-up switches, each signifying a potential multibillion-dollar opportunity over their lifetimes.

Marvell ended the quarter with $4.96 billion in debt, but its net debt was low compared to its earnings at just 0.27 times EBITDA. Because Marvell will use its own shares, not cash, to buy Lumentum, current shareholders will own a smaller stake in the combined company. Still, Marvell will have to manage Lumentum's debt and other financial responsibilities while integrating the two businesses and keeping its own operations and growth on track.

How to Play MRVL Stock Now

Marvell has an attractive opportunity to become a bigger player in AI connectivity and challenge Broadcom, but the Lumentum deal raises the execution stakes. Marvell still has to show it can integrate this major acquisition, manage dilution, and turn its new technology into real, profitable growth.

MRVL offers substantial upside, but the acquisition raises the bar for successful integration and growth. Investors confident in Marvell's ability could build exposure gradually around quarterly results and deal updates. More cautious investors might prefer to wait for clearer proof before investing.

Overall, analysts continue to be strongly bullish about MRVL stock. Of the 37 analysts covering the stock, 26 rate it a "Strong Buy," three a "Moderate Buy," and eight a "Hold." Marvell's average price target of $307.88 indicates a possible upside of 111%. The most ambitious forecast of $450 hints at an exciting 208% upside from the current price.

news.Title: Lumentum, Corning, and other optical-related stocks jump on Chinese import restrictions
news.Content:
US optical equipment stocks popped on Tuesday after reports that the Trump administration plans to move forward with restrictions on imports of Chinese data center equipment.

Coherent ( COHR ) rose 3%, and Applied Optoelectronics ( AAOI ), Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ), and Corning ( GLW ) all advanced roughly 2%, as US data centers would be forced to turn to US suppliers amid the tighter measure.

According to Reuters, the proposed rules target new models of Chinese optical transceivers that enable high-speed data transmission in data centers. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has flagged concerns that the equipment could be used to steal data or hack US data centers.

The measure is moving forward despite opposition from Amazon ( AMZN ), Google ( GOOGL ), Meta ( META ), and other US tech companies, according to the report.

The tighter restrictions follow US export controls on advanced chips announced on Monday. The US Commerce Department's new rule requires licenses for certain advanced semiconductor exports to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. The rule is aimed at preventing US AI chip restrictions from being circumvented via overseas data centers and remote access, which could give Chinese companies access to the technology.

On Tuesday, Chinese stocks Alibaba ( BABA ) and Baidu ( BIDU ) extended losses from the prior session, declining more than 3% and 2%, respectively.

Separately, on Tuesday, Nvidia ( NVDA ) said its board had created a new committee to oversee national security policies, export controls, and global trade risks.

The announcement came ahead of the company's earnings release Tuesday as scrutiny of its semiconductors and export practices has intensified following the resignation of Jensen Huang. The former CEO acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife after reports that he had extramarital affairs, including with a woman reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy.

Nvidia stock ticked down after falling more than 4% in the prior session.

news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Keeps On Going Down
news.Content:
For Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) investors, the bad news is a little less bad on Tuesday.

Ever since Nvidia's CEO resigned , the stock has been sliding. Shares of the GPU AI chips giant are now down about 25% for the month of November. (The good news is that as of 1:10 p.m. ET, Nvidia stock is down only about 1.5% more today.)

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

For Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) investors, the news is quite a bit worse. Not only is Sandisk stock down 32% in November. It's also down more than Nvidia stock today -- 2.7%.

Image source: Getty Images.

What's ailing Sandisk

Why are investors so down on Sandisk stock, whose own CEO -- unlike Nvidia's ex-CEO -- has not yet admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese Communist spy?

As I explained yesterday, Sandisk's problems basically stem from the fact that Nvidia AI chips and Sandisk's NAND flash memory chips are sold in pairs. You can't build an AI data center without both of them, and so if demand for Nvidia chips drops because of this scandal, Sandisk's sales might also suffer.

What's next for Sandisk

Granted, there's also the possibility that Sandisk might not take any hit at all. Nvidia's chip sales might not suffer after all, and even if they do, other producers of AI chips, such as AMD or Intel , might pick up the slack. In either of those situations, Sandisk's memory chips should still be in demand.

But here's the latest bad news: As my fellow Fool Travis Hoium reports, semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis thinks capital spending on AI chips in 2027 could be 19% below previous estimates, 2028 spending might be 28% below, and 2029 spending could fall 41 % below estimates.

How bad is this news? Well, luckily, it still works out to 24% annual sales growth in AI chips over the next five years. At a forward P/E ratio less than 4.0, and a PEG ratio less than 0.2 (!), I remain bullish on Sandisk stock.

KLAC Jumps 28% in a Year: What's Driving the Stock?

KLA shares have returned 28% in the trailing 12 months, outperforming the broader sector. Despite its premium valuation, the company's strong position in semiconductor process control, accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, rising demand for advanced packaging solutions and robust cash flow generation support its growth prospects.

The company is benefiting from increasing investments in AI infrastructure, which are driving demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing and process control solutions. The transition toward more complex chip architectures and leading-edge manufacturing nodes is increasing inspection and metrology requirements. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, semiconductor process control revenues increased 29% year over year to $3.75 billion, while wafer inspection revenues surged 37% to $2.11 billion.

KLAC expects the wafer fabrication equipment market, including advanced packaging, to reach the mid-$150 billion range in 2026 and exceed $200 billion in 2027. KLA's growing exposure to advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) represents a significant growth catalyst. Increasing adoption of heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging architectures is creating additional inspection and process control requirements. The company expects advanced packaging process control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in 2026, suggesting more than 70% year-over-year growth, nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced packaging market.

KLA's expanding installed base and increasing semiconductor manufacturing complexity are driving sustained demand for services. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, services revenues increased 14% year over year to $850 million, accounting for approximately 20% of total revenues. Strong demand reflects increasing equipment utilization, longer tool life cycles and customers' growing emphasis on productivity, yield optimization and system availability.

However, KLA continues to face supply chain constraints that could limit its ability to capitalize fully on accelerating semiconductor equipment demand. The company highlighted shortages of critical optical components and other long-lead-time materials, with average equipment lead times extending to approximately 12 months and certain advanced systems requiring even longer. KLA is also facing profitability challenges from persistently elevated memory costs, particularly DRAM used in its systems' image-processing capabilities. The company expects second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP gross margin of 62.5%, slightly below the 62.7% reported in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and its long-term target range of 63-64%.

The company's share price performance has suffered from these challenges. KLA shares have underperformed MKS, Lam Research and Entegris in a year's time. Shares of MKS, Lam Research and Entegris have returned 45.6%, 47.2% and 92.4%, respectively.

news.Title: Is It Worth Investing in KLA (KLAC) Based on Wall Street's Bullish Views?
news.Content:
The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about KLA (KLAC) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

KLA currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.73, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 28 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.73 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 28 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 16 are Strong Buy and three are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 57.1% and 10.7% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for KLAC

Check price target & stock forecast for KLA here>>>

The ABR suggests buying KLA, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

On the other hand, earnings estimate revisions are at the core of the Zacks Rank. And empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates. In other words, this tool always maintains a balance among its five ranks.

There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices.

Is KLAC a Good Investment?

In terms of earnings estimate revisions for KLA, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 5.4% over the past month to $5.73.

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for KLA. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, the Buy-equivalent ABR for KLA may serve as a useful guide for investors.

news.Title: ASML vs. Lam Research: Which Chipmaking Stock is the Better Buy Now?
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. ASML and Lam Research Corporation LRCX are two premier technology firms benefiting from AI-driven chip demand and investments in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Both players are well-positioned to benefit from growing demand for advanced computing, with ASML supplying the lithography equipment essential for manufacturing semiconductors and Lam Research supplying wafer fabrication equipment and related services.

ASML provides sophisticated hardware, software and systems that enable semiconductor manufacturers to produce increasingly smaller, faster and more energy-efficient chips. Its technologies are primarily used in the lithography stage of semiconductor manufacturing, in which complex circuit patterns are transferred onto silicon wafers.

Lam Research caters to the needs of semiconductor memory, foundry and integrated device manufacturers by providing them with integrated hardware, process, materials, software and process control. It serves the related markets that rely on semiconductor processes and require production-proven manufacturing capabilities, such as complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor image sensors and micro-electromechanical systems.

Let us try to analyze some of the competitive strengths and weaknesses of the companies to understand who is in a better position to maximize gains from the emerging market trends.

The Case for ASML

Rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is one of ASML's most powerful growth drivers. Training and inference workloads require increasingly powerful and energy-efficient processors, which are accelerating the transition toward smaller process nodes and more advanced memory technologies. The ongoing investments and continued progress in AI technologies are further boosting demand for both advanced Logic and Memory chips. Semiconductor manufacturers are accelerating capacity expansion plans, resulting in stronger commitments across ASML's product portfolio.

ASML's decision to materially increase manufacturing capacity further indicates stronger demand visibility. Based on strong customer commitments, the company expects to ship about 65 low-NA EUV systems in 2026, more than 50% above 2025, while DUV immersion shipments should be approximately in line with 2025. Management targets 30% additional capacity in 2027 and a significant increase in 2028 in tune with customer demand. Capacity expansion suggests customers are giving ASML greater visibility into their multi-year fab and technology plans.

However, management attributes the current demand environment primarily to AI-related investment and the resulting need for more advanced Logic and Memory capacity. Although this has produced unusually long order visibility for ASML, it makes the growth profile increasingly dependent on customers maintaining those expansion plans. A slower pace of customer investment would therefore affect both system demand and utilization of the larger production footprint ASML is preparing, resulting in elevated operational risks.

Story Continues

The Case for LRCX

Lam Research is extending its foundry and logic capabilities into advanced DRAM as customers adopt more demanding patterns and materials processes. The company has high exposure to memory, where AI is increasing storage and bandwidth requirements. Management expects 2026 wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending in the mid-$150 billion range and preliminary 2027 spending above $200 billion. DRAM is expected to lead percentage growth, followed by leading-edge foundry/logic and NAND. LRCX expects NAND demand across QLC, TLC and emerging SLC-class storage tiers to expand wafer capacity requirements. Its extensive NAND installed base supports opportunities from both technology upgrades and capacity additions.

AI workloads are increasing demand for HBM, chiplets and advanced packaging. Lam Research expects advanced packaging to remain a major growth driver as customers adopt more complex interconnects, through-silicon vias and bonding technologies. Its Syndion etch platform secured four new positions across multiple customers in advanced logic and HBM applications. Striker ALD also achieved multiple TSV liner wins, while VECTOR and TEOS 3D gained positions in bonding films and inter-die gap-fill applications. Lam Research has shipped panel plating systems to more than 20 customers across panel sizes ranging from 300-by-300 millimeters to 600-by-600 millimeters. Management expects its panel-level packaging market position eventually to exceed its established wafer-level packaging position.

However, semiconductor equipment demand remains cyclical and depends on customer capital budgets, end-market conditions and new fab construction. Although management expects WFE spending above $200 billion in 2027, limited cleanroom availability and component supply constraints could prevent equipment manufacturers from meeting demand fully. Trade restrictions and export controls remain a material risk because China contributed 35% of September-quarter 2026 revenues, increasing from 26% in June. The September increase reflected investment by both domestic and multinational customers, including mature-node foundry spending. However, management expects China's revenue contribution to decline substantially in the December quarter.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for ASML & LRCX?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ASML's 2026 sales implies year-over-year growth of 33.9%, while that for EPS indicates a surge of 66.4%. The EPS estimates have trended up 5.3% over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lam Research's fiscal 2027 sales indicates a year-over-year growth of 49.9%, while that for EPS suggests a rise of 65.2%. The EPS estimates have trended up 3% over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of ASML & LRCX

Over the past year, Lam Research has jumped 47.1% compared with the industry's growth of 10.8%. ASML has gained 40.1% over the same period.

Lam Research looks more attractive than ASML from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, ASML's shares currently trade at 8.81 forward sales, higher than 7.05 for Lam Research.

ASML or LRCX: Which is a Better Pick?

Lam Research currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), while ASML has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Both ASML and LRCX expect revenues and earnings to improve in the current fiscal. In terms of price performance, ASML has outperformed Lam Research, though it is trading at a slight premium. With a better Zacks Rank and solid fundamentals, ASML appears to be relatively better placed than Lam Research and is, therefore, a stronger investment option at the moment.

news.Content:
Investing.com -- Shares of US optical technology companies rallied on Tuesday after Reuters reported that the Trump administration plans to move forward with efforts to restrict imports of Chinese data center equipment despite opposition from major US technology companies.

The proposed restrictions target new models of Chinese optical transceivers, which enable high-speed data transmission over fiber-optic cables inside data centers. The Federal Communications Commission has raised national security concerns that the equipment could potentially be used to steal data, install malware or disrupt US data center operations.

According to Reuters, the initiative is moving forward despite lobbying from Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave, Cisco and Microsoft. The industry has also raised concerns about potential Chinese retaliation. US companies reportedly warned that Beijing could restrict exports of indium phosphide, a critical material used in manufacturing optical transceivers.

The latest developments could strengthen the position of domestic optical equipment manufacturers if restrictions force US data center operators to shift orders away from Chinese suppliers.

"My preference has been to move in slow, steady increments, consistently, successively at meetings to make sure we're getting that policy restriction back in the economy to help bring inflation back down to our 2% objective," Hammack said.

Story Continues

U.S. rate futures are currently pricing in a 95.4% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike and a 4.6% chance of a 50-basis-point rate hike at the December FOMC meeting.

Today, investors will closely watch earnings from AI bellwether Nvidia (NVDA). The chipmaker's results are typically a key test for the AI trade and the broader market, but they are likely to draw even more attention this time following the dramatic downfall of former CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang. Nvidia is scheduled to report its Q3 results after the closing bell. While the numbers will be closely scrutinized, the main focus will be on how the company plans to move forward and whether it can sustain its extraordinary growth without Huang, dubbed the "godfather of AI." The report comes after Nvidia shares fell again on Monday, extending a selloff sparked by Huang's resignation following revelations of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy and reports of another relationship with an Nvidia employee.

Still, StoneX's Cody Acree said that strong earnings should spark a rebound in Nvidia's battered shares. "We expect a strong guide, and steady messaging should be enough to spur a relief rally, as investors try to time a bottom," Acree said. Options pricing implies a 7.10% move in NVDA shares in either direction by Wednesday's close, based on 85% of the value of the at-the-money straddle, according to Barchart.

Before Nvidia's earnings, investors will focus on U.S. retail sales data, set to be released in a couple of hours. Economists forecast that retail sales will show a +0.1% m/m increase in October after a +0.8% m/m gain in September. Core retail sales, which exclude motor vehicles and parts, are estimated to rise +0.4% m/m in October after climbing +0.9% m/m in September.

U.S. industrial production and manufacturing production data will also be released today. Economists project industrial production to be unchanged m/m and manufacturing production to rise +0.2% m/m in October, compared with September's figures of +0.7% m/m and +0.3% m/m, respectively.

The U.S. import and export price indexes will be released today as well. Economists expect the import price index to climb +0.7% m/m and the export price index to rise +0.3% m/m in October, compared with the previous month's figures of +1.1% m/m and +2.2% m/m, respectively.

In addition, market participants will parse comments from Fed Governor Christopher Waller, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, and New York Fed President John Williams today.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is at 5.12%, down -0.33%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 Index is down -0.85% this morning as a selloff in technology shares dampened sentiment ahead of Nvidia's high-stakes earnings. Tech shares slumped on Tuesday after Washington moved to restrict China's access to advanced AI computing. Mining stocks also sank, hit by lower metal prices. In addition, bank stocks declined, dragged down by a drop of more than -4% in Deutsche Bank (DBK.D.DX) following a string of media reports based on millions of internal documents leaked by whistleblowers. The ZEW Economic Institute reported on Tuesday that German investor sentiment jumped in November, reaching its highest level since the outbreak of the Iran war. "The German economy remains on its recovery track, albeit moving at a slow rate," said ZEW President Achim Wambach. Separately, data showed that U.K. annual wage growth eased in the three months through September, while the unemployment rate unexpectedly fell, a combination unlikely to deter the Bank of England from raising interest rates. In addition, final data showed that Italy's annual inflation rate picked up more than initially estimated in October. Meanwhile, the European Commission said on Tuesday that the Eurozone economy has proven more resilient than anticipated this year, supported by external demand, and is expected to maintain moderate growth in 2027 and 2028. The Commission, in its new forecasts, projected Eurozone economic growth of 1.2% this year, matching the pace of 2025 and marking an upgrade from its May estimate of 0.9%. In other corporate news, Avio SpA (AVIO.M.DX) jumped over +12% after Finnish company Iceye Oy made a takeover bid for the firm.

U.K. Average Earnings ex Bonus, U.K. Unemployment Rate, Italy's CPI, Germany's ZEW Economic Sentiment Index, and Eurozone's ZEW Economic Sentiment Index were released today.

U.K. Average Earnings ex Bonus rose 3.5% in the three months to September, in line with expectations.

The U.K. Unemployment Rate was 4.6% in the three months to September, stronger than expectations of no change at 4.7%.

The Italian October CPI rose +1.0% m/m and +5.5% y/y, stronger than expectations of +0.9% m/m and +5.4% y/y.

The German November ZEW Economic Sentiment Index came in at 35.6, stronger than expectations of 28.8.

The Eurozone November ZEW Economic Sentiment Index arrived at 26.5, stronger than expectations of 19.1.

Asian stock markets closed in the red today. China's Shanghai Composite Index ($CHSC) closed down -0.50%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index ($NKY) closed down -1.34%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index closed lower today as investors assessed the implications of stricter U.S. curbs on China's access to top AI chips and looked ahead to the APEC summit. AI-related stocks slumped on Tuesday after the U.S. moved to restrict several countries from giving Chinese companies remote access to advanced AI chips and servers. The restrictions followed a scandal involving Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Chinese AI firms could face higher model-training costs and slower growth in cloud revenue as a result of the crackdown, analysts said. At the same time, semiconductor stocks rallied on expectations that the curbs would speed up the development of domestic alternatives. Meanwhile, official data released on Tuesday showed that foreign investors increased their holdings of China's onshore yuan bonds in October. In corporate news, Baidu fell over -5% in Hong Kong after the search-engine giant reported weaker-than-expected Q3 profit. Investor focus is now on the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' summit in Shenzhen, where U.S. President Donald Trump is set to hold the third of four planned one-on-one meetings this year with Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Thursday, followed by a trilateral meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Attention will then turn to the People's Bank of China, which is set to announce the country's benchmark lending rates on Friday. Economists expect the one-year loan prime rate to stay unchanged at 3.00% and the five-year LPR at 3.50%.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index closed lower today, tracking overnight losses on Wall Street. Chip-related and other AI-linked stocks slid on Tuesday as U.S. efforts to curb China's access to advanced AI chips and servers added to investor caution ahead of Nvidia's earnings. Memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings sank over -5%, chip-testing equipment maker Advantest fell more than -4%, and tech investor SoftBank Group dropped over -3%, putting significant pressure on the Nikkei. Losses in bank stocks also weighed on the benchmark. Meanwhile, Japanese government bond yields were mixed on Tuesday. Elsewhere, Reuters reported on Tuesday that Japan's Ministry of Finance will likely delay the launch of a new type of floating-rate government bond as it reviews whether investor demand is sufficient. Investor focus for the remainder of the week is on Japan's national core CPI for October, which is expected to show that price pressures firmed. Japan's October trade data and September core machinery orders figures will also attract attention. The Nikkei Volatility Index, which takes into account the implied volatility of Nikkei 225 options, closed up +9.94% at 38.59.

Pre-Market U.S. Stock Movers

Most chip and AI infrastructure stocks advanced in pre-market trading, recovering some of their losses after a two-session rout. Marvell Technology (MRVL) was up over +4%, while Arm Holdings (ARM) and Micron Technology (MU) each rose more than +1%.

Intel (INTC) slid over -2% in pre-market trading after a regulatory filing revealed that Nvidia reduced its stake in the chipmaker by 25% in the third quarter.

Cisco Systems (CSCO) rose more than +1% in pre-market trading after DZ Bank and HSBC upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold.

Red Cat Holdings (RCAT) tanked over -33% in pre-market trading after the defense drone maker posted downbeat Q3 results and withdrew its full-year revenue guidance.

PepsiCo (PEP) fell nearly -2% in pre-market trading after Bernstein downgraded the stock to Underperform from Market Perform with a price target of $128.

news.Title: 5檔ETF換股！00940「10進10出」 刪英業達、聯發科增南亞科
繼續拚AI！兆豐銀等10銀行 完成力積電300億元聯貸
news.Content:
面對全球人工智慧（AI）浪潮帶動半導體產業加速升級轉型，金融業亦透過資金支持與永續金融機制，協助企業強化競爭力並實現淨零轉型。由兆豐銀行統籌，與合作金庫銀行、華南銀行、彰化銀行及台灣土地銀行共同主辦之力晶積成電子製造股份有限公司300億元聯貸，今17日由力積電董事長暨執行長謝再居與兆豐銀行董事長董瑞斌完成簽約。

兆豐銀表示，共計10家金融機構踴躍參與，展現銀行團對力積電營運轉型及長期發展的支持。資金用途主要為償還金融機構借款，以及支應購置機器設備、興建、改建或購置廠房暨充實中期營運資金所需。此外，本案結合力積電持續推動節能減碳、減廢及資源循環之永續作為，將「節能率」、「廢棄物再利用率」及「製程用水回收率」三項ESG指標與授信條件連結，鼓勵力積電持續提升永續績效，實踐營運發展與環境永續並進。

隨著全球半導體產業朝人工智慧、高效能運算等應用快速發展，力積電近年積極調整營運及產品布局，持續深化記憶體、邏輯晶圓代工及3D AI Foundry等業務，並與國際記憶體大廠美光深化策略合作，推進HBM後段晶圓製造及記憶體製程技術合作，同時布局晶圓堆疊(WoW)、中介層(Interposer)及矽電容晶圓等AI應用領域，持續優化產品組合及營運體質。本次聯貸案將有助力積電整合中長期資金資源，支應後續營運轉型與技術發展所需，進一步強化長期競爭力。

兆豐銀行深耕聯貸市場多年，長期支持國內半導體、科技製造及重大產業發展，未來兆豐銀行將持續發揮金融核心職能，攜手優質企業掌握科技創新、產業升級及全球布局契機，共創穩健且永續之成長動能。

news.Title: 兆豐00913換股「3進3出」 南亞科、全新、精材入列搶攻AI商機
news.Content:
台股ETF迎來新一波成分股調整！兆豐台灣晶圓製造(00913-TW)將於今(17)日進行下半年成分股調整，採取「3進3出」，新納入南亞科(2408-TW)、全新(2455-TW)及精材(3374-TW)，刪除光洋科(1785-TW)、志聖(2467-TW)及精測(6510-TW)，調整結果於今日收盤後生效。此次新納入標的橫跨記憶體、光通訊及先進封裝領域，瞄準AI資料中心與高效能運算帶動的半導體供應鏈商機。

觀察此次新增的3檔成分股，各自掌握不同AI關鍵應用。南亞科為台灣DRAM製造大廠，可望受惠AI伺服器推升記憶體需求；全新為砷化鎵磊晶片廠，布局資料中心高速光通訊及矽光子傳輸所需的關鍵材料；精材則為台積電轉投資的晶圓封裝廠，切入3D感測及先進封測領域，隨著AI晶片朝高效能、高整合度發展，相關技術需求也備受市場關注。

兆豐00913投資團隊指出，近期全球AI晶片龍頭輝達(NVIDIA)傳出高層人事變動及相關調查消息，引發市場對接班布局、技術路線及核心供應鏈變化的關注。不過，從整體產業鏈來看，無論未來AI晶片設計版圖如何變化，主流AI晶片與高效能運算處理器仍高度仰賴台灣在晶圓製造、先進製程及高階封裝的技術優勢。

法人分析，隨著市場評估AI產業未來發展，雲端服務供應商(CSP)可能進一步分散晶片供應來源，擴大與超微(AMD)、博通(Broadcom)及各大廠自研ASIC晶片的合作。面對AI晶片設計大廠之間的競爭與市場資金快速輪動，單押特定個股可能面臨較大的波動風險，透過ETF配置半導體供應鏈，則可分散個別公司的投資風險。

兆豐00913聚焦台灣晶圓製造與半導體產業，此次成分股調整也納入記憶體、光通訊及先進封測等AI供應鏈環節。投資團隊認為，無論未來AI晶片訂單流向哪一家國際設計大廠，台灣晶圓製造及高階封測供應鏈仍是產業發展的重要核心。

news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者劉居全報導】近期全球AI晶片龍頭輝達（NVIDIA）傳出高層領導變動與相關調查消息，引發市場高度關注其後續接班布局、技術路線圖演進及核心供應鏈的動態重組。聚焦台灣半導體與晶圓製造核心優勢的兆豐台灣晶圓製造(00913)投資團隊指出，面對科技巨頭人事更迭與市場不確定性，相較於單押個股的波動風險，透過ETF進行一籃子股票配置，更能發揮風險分散、平衡布局與緊扣產業大趨勢的多重優勢。隨著市場提前為「後黃仁勳時代」進行評估與定價，法人分析指出，輝達高層異動短期內可能使較為積極的研發與規格迭代節奏略為放緩，進而牽動雲端服務供應商加速分散供應鏈，擴大對超微、博通及各大廠自研ASIC的合作布局。然而，從整體產業鏈結構觀察，無論未來AI晶片設計權與市占率如何在國際大廠間重新洗牌，所有主流AI晶片與高效能運算處理器，皆高度仰賴台灣作為全球最核心的製造、先進製程與高階封測基地。

在指數調整方面，兆豐00913今(17)日進行下半年成分股調整並於當日收盤生效，本次新納入南亞科(2408)、全新(2455)及精材(3374)，同時刪除光洋科(1785)、志聖(2467)及精測(6510)。此次新納入的三檔標的皆在半導體生態系擁有關鍵地位，包括台灣DRAM製造龍頭南亞科，受惠於AI帶動記憶體需求強勁；全球砷化鎵磊晶片大廠全新，掌握資料中心高速光通訊與矽光子傳輸關鍵材料；以及台積電轉投資的晶圓封裝大廠精材，切入3D感測與先進封測商機。

news.Title: Lumentum (LITE) Got a Takeover Offer. What Does It Mean for Holders? (
news.Content:
Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE ) took the 10th spot on our latest list, 11 Unstoppable Stocks to Buy According to Analysts .

AI stocks had a brutal week. Last Thursday, the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, its biggest one-day drop since the April 2025 tariff shock. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost more than 1,800 points, and the Nasdaq Composite tumbled 5.5%. The slide erased the market's gain from the day before, its best in three months. Stock markets around the world felt the pressure, and South Korea's Kospi index fell 5.3%.

The Nasdaq slid into a correction, the term Wall Street uses for a drop of more than 10% from a recent peak. Volatility spiked as well. Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX, posted its biggest one-day jump in over two years, Futurum Equities chief market strategist Shay Boloor pointed out.

Stocks tied to the buildout of AI data centers led the slide. Investors had cheered the midterm election results a day earlier, then turned anxious about what a Democratic Congress could mean for the spending that feeds those data centers. We covered the group's earlier pullback in our list of oversold AI stocks that Wall Street analysts saw 50%+ upside in , published before the selloff.

Goldman Sachs estimates that about 45% of planned US data center capacity now faces possible restrictions, after newly elected state governors promised to stop or pause construction, Yahoo Finance reported.

AI stocks had already been swinging for months on worries that building more data centers may slow because borrowing has become so expensive. Last month, Baird tech strategist Ted Mortonson said the selloff is increasingly about who needs financing and what that financing costs. Chip stocks took the hardest hit, in their worst selloff since 2020, and about $3 trillion in stock market value vanished in a single session.

Stocks recovered some ground. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq rebounded on Friday, and on Wednesday each climbed more than 1% as the semiconductor index jumped 7%, Reuters reported. Readers who follow the group can find more names in our list of the best semiconductor stocks to buy for the next decade .

Government bond yields remain a worry. The 10-year Treasury yield was hovering around 5.0% this week, a level that keeps pressure on stocks that are priced for fast growth. On Thursday, the Nasdaq slipped 0.4% as the 10-year yield rose to 5.09%, Yahoo Finance reported, as investors weighed the odds of more Federal Reserve rate hikes.

Lumentum made it to our list because it has an average upside potential of 69% and a 1-year performance of 175.13%. Lumentum makes the lasers and optical parts that carry data between AI servers, and its sales more than doubled over the year. Revenue was $1.26 billion in the fiscal first quarter, against $533.8 million a year earlier. Chief Executive Officer Michael Hurlston said growth came across all of its businesses, led by pump lasers and optical circuit switches.

Story Continues

Guidance points higher still. For the fiscal second quarter, Lumentum expects revenue of $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion, and it projects an operating margin that would be its highest yet.

Then came a takeover offer. Marvell agreed to acquire the company in an all-stock deal at a fixed ratio of 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share. The companies said that implied about $1,132 per share before talks were reported, and because payment is in stock, the value moves with Marvell's shares. Lumentum holders would own about 33% of the combined company, and Marvell Chief Executive Officer Matt Murphy would lead it. Hurlston said the combination creates a category leader in AI connectivity, with long-term value well above what Lumentum could deliver alone. Demand that outruns supply is the theme of our analysis of whether Lumentum's valuation can hold up .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of SNDK as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk.
