news.Title: Why Arm Holdings Plunged Today
news.Content:
Shares of Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) fell on Monday, down 7.9% as of 3:45 p.m. EDT.

Arm certainly wasn't alone, as pretty much the entire sector fell hard on the day due to several factors, all of which relate to uncertainty over the AI build-out and specifically the fate of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) within the AI ecosystem.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Arm's downturn today may have been particularly severe due to its close relationship with Nvidia as a licensor for Nvidia's CPUs.

No chipmaker escapes the semiconductor downturn

Semiconductor stocks were down sharply today, with some, like Arm Holdings, down more than others. There are likely a few reasons driving this sell-off.

First, a prominent semiconductor and AI research firm, SemiAnalysis, reportedly issued a forecast update to institutional clients over the weekend, downgrading its prior growth forecast for AI accelerators through 2030. These cuts were relatively significant, with cuts to accelerator revenue estimates of 19%, 28%, 41%, and 40% for 2027 through 2030, respectively, compared with prior expectations.

It should be noted that even with these cuts, SemiAnalysis still forecasts growth every year through 2030, just not as much. Furthermore, the cuts seem to bring SemiAnalysis' estimates more in line with Wall Street analysts'. However, the devil is in the details: the bulk of the cuts to estimates appear to be due to Nvidia chip pricing, while competitive vendors were less affected.

Combined with the fact that Nvidia reports earnings tomorrow in what will likely be a hugely consequential report without former CEO Jensen Huang, investors are understandably de-risking by selling the entire chip ecosystem today.

For Arm specifically, Nvidia licenses Arm's technology to produce its CPUs, the latest of which is named Vera. While CPUs weren't part of SemiAnalysis' report, which focused on accelerators and GPUs, the association with Nvidia could be affecting Arm more than other chip stocks today. Oh, and starting from a high-looking valuation of 77.5 times forward earnings, even after today's sell-off, likely didn't help.

Image source: Getty Images.

Arm has a promising future but is still expensive

To be sure, Arm has customers other than Nvidia. In fact, virtually all major hyperscaler cloud companies license Arm's architecture for their custom CPUs. Furthermore, Arm has its own AGI CPU coming, with initial sales forecast to begin at the end of next year.

Story Continues

That's all very promising; however, Arm's high valuation relative to some other semiconductor companies likely means there are better buys available, especially after the sector's major sell-off over the past two months .

news.Title: Top 5 Stocks that Have Survived Major Founder Transitions
news.Content:
Several events could test a company, and the exit of its founder is right up there as one of the most notable ones. The analyst community, as well as the broader market, could react disproportionately to the situation, which reflects on how closely investors tie a company's prospects to the individual who built it all.

Founders are not just the company executives. They actually lay out the organizational culture, its overall strategy, and often are the face of a company. Many times, the market prices in a "founder premium" for the risk-taking ability that professional investment managers might avoid. You also might want to check out our 10 Buy the Dip Stocks Insiders Are Loading Up On After the Recent Market Sell-Off .

When such an individual departs, the market reaction entails a very critical question. It is whether the business's success is attributed to the individual or to the system built around them. The context of these departures carries significance, as some founders leave by choice, while others are forced due to some controversy. Insider Monkey also compiled a list of stocks likely to benefit from interest rate hikes . See the full list here.

Historically, we have seen signs of both warnings and reassurances following such departures. Some businesses lose their way, drifting away without any vision. Others have found that a strong successor, a deep bench, and disciplined processes can carry a business well beyond its creator. With that background, let's explore our Top 10 Stocks that Have Survived Major Founder Transitions.

We provided the expanded list of Top 10 Stocks that Have Survived Major Founder Transitions . The top 5 stocks are listed below.

Methodology:

news.Title: ARM's 50% Licensing Revenue Surge Signals Strong AI-Driven Demand
news.Content:
Arm Holdings plc ARM reported robust licensing revenue growth in second-quarter fiscal 2027, underscoring sustained demand for its chip designs and intellectual property. The company's expanding presence in artificial intelligence (AI), cloud infrastructure and advanced computing continues to strengthen its growth prospects.

Licensing and other revenues jumped 50% year over year to $773 million, becoming a major contributor to ARM's quarterly performance. This momentum reflects growing customer interest in advanced semiconductor technologies.

ARM's Licensing Momentum Fuels Revenue Growth

ARM's total revenues increased 27% year over year to $1.44 billion, supported by expanding licensing activity and steady royalty contributions.

The licensing business benefited from strong demand for Arm Holdings' intellectual property, alongside sizable agreements and the conversion of previously secured contracts into recognized revenues.

Growing investments in AI infrastructure and customized processors present additional opportunities for ARM to capitalize on its technology portfolio.

However, the timing of major licensing agreements can create fluctuations in quarterly revenues, potentially affecting near-term growth consistency.

Royalty Opportunities Strengthen ARM's Outlook

Royalty revenues increased 8% year over year to $670 million, supported by wider adoption of advanced chip architectures and growing deployment of Arm-based processors in data centers.

Increasing adoption of Armv9 and Compute Subsystems (CSS) supports higher royalty potential per chip, strengthening ARM's longer-term monetization opportunities.

Nevertheless, smartphone market pressures associated with memory pricing remain a concern.

Overall, Arm Holdings' licensing performance highlights its expanding influence across semiconductor markets. Sustained demand for advanced processor designs, combined with improving royalty economics, could support continued revenue growth despite licensing volatility and smartphone-related uncertainties.

How Do ARM's Industry Peers Compare?

NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices AMD are two prominent U.S.-listed semiconductor companies benefiting from expanding AI infrastructure investments.

NVIDIA continues to capitalize on demand for AI accelerators and integrated computing platforms, strengthening its position in data center infrastructure. Its extensive software ecosystem provides competitive advantages in AI deployment.

AMD is expanding its presence in AI accelerators and server processors, supported by growing demand for high-performance computing solutions.

Story Continues

Unlike NVIDIA and AMD, ARM primarily monetizes semiconductor designs through licensing and royalties, giving it exposure to multiple chip manufacturers without directly competing in processor manufacturing.

Both NVIDIA and AMD face intense competition and evolving customer requirements.

ARM's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Arm Holdings stock has surged 74.3% year to date, significantly outperforming the industry's 8.1% gain.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

From a valuation standpoint, ARM trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 27.03X, well above the industry's 3.01X. It carries a Value Score of F.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company's fiscal 2027 earnings has increased to $2.24 per share over the past 60 days.

ARM currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Could Big Buybacks Be the Next Catalyst for These 3 AI Stocks?
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Lam Research Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

AI stocks sold off after Democrats' midterm election wins raised concerns about data center opposition, though many names have since partially recovered.

Lam Research, Dynatrace, and EMCOR Group all remain well below their 52-week highs and recently announced major new share buyback authorizations.

Monitoring next quarter's buyback spending at these firms could reveal whether they capitalized on the recent dip or grew cautious about AI growth.

AI stocks have gone on a rollercoaster ride lately. After Democrats' sweeping midterm election victories, investors worried that changes in political leadership could lead to greater opposition to data center construction and project delays. However, many AI stocks have bounced back swiftly after tanking on Nov. 5.

Nonetheless, many names remain down significantly from their 52-week highs. This includes semiconductor manufacturing equipment company Lam Research (NASDAQ: LRCX), AI-linked software company Dynatrace (NYSE: DT), and construction and engineering company EMCOR Group (NYSE: EME).

→ 3 Large-Cap Stocks Are Outperforming the S&P 500 Without AI Hype

These three companies all recently made significant buyback announcements. With shares still down significantly, these firms could buy back shares at lower levels and add a tailwind to per-share metrics.

Lam Adds $25 Billion in Buyback Capacity With Shares Down Over 45%

Midway through 2026, shares of Lam Research peaked, putting the stock up around 155%. However, the stock has now fallen more than 45% from its 52-week high. The company continues to post strong financial performance. Last quarter, Lam's sales increased by 54% year over year (YOY), one of the company's highest growth rates over the past 10 years.

→ Embraer's Record Backlog Looks Promising, But Can It Keep Its Margins Climbing?

Notably, on Nov. 5, Lam authorized a $25 billion share buyback program. This program is very large in relation to Lam's market capitalization near $282 billion, representing around 8.8% of the company's value. Lam also said during its last earnings call that it still had $3 billion under its previous repurchase authorization. Adding in this figure boosts the company's buyback capacity to around 10% of its market capitalization.

Together, these programs give Lam significant ability to continue lowering its share count over time. Although Lam's share count has remained relatively stable over the last 12 months, the company has greatly reduced its share count over a longer period. Since the end of 2021, the firm's outstanding shares have fallen by around 11%, now sitting at approximately 1.25 billion.

Story Continues

→ Modine Manufacturing Scales Up to Solve the AI Heat Problem

Dynatrace's Buyback Capacity Hits 10% of Market Cap

Dynatrace is one of the top players in the observability software market. Observability is becoming increasingly important as agentic AI proliferates because it allows companies to track and correct the performance of their AI agents. Partially driven by the company's agentic AI opportunity, shares were up as much as 50% year-to-date in mid-October.

However, Dynatrace shares came tumbling down after its latest earnings report as the firm's net new annual recurring revenue was flat YOY, falling below expectations. Shares are now up just slightly on the year, and have fallen around 30% from their 52-week high.

The company also announced a $1 billion buyback authorization, bringing its total buyback capacity to $1.3 billion. This is equal to a very hefty 10.2% of the firm's approximately $12.7 billion market capitalization. Dynatrace's history of lowering its share count is relatively short, but the company has made significant progress recently. From the end of 2021 to the end of 2025, Dynatrace's share count increased by nearly 6% to 301 million. Since then, its share count has dropped by more than 4%.

The company's large buyback capacity could help it continue this trend, and Dynatrace plans to share more details on its capital allocation framework in February 2027.

EMCOR Increases Buyback Authorization; Data Center Demand Drives Record Performance Obligations

EMCOR Group has been a significant beneficiary of data center demand, with AI tailwinds helping its growth accelerate. Last quarter, sales increased by 28.8% YOY, setting a quarterly revenue record. Driven by data centers, EMCOR's remaining performance obligations hit a record $18.57 billion, an increase of 47% YOY.

However, the stock has plummeted from its highs in May, when shares were up as much as 54% year-to-date. EMCOR shares remain up around 8% in 2026, with the stock down 30% from its high.

The company also announced a $500 million addition to its share repurchase authorization during its last earnings report. This represents around 1.7% of the company's market capitalization, which sits near $29 billion. While relatively small compared to Lam and Dynatrace's programs, it still allows the company to put downward pressure on its share count.

Like Lam, EMCOR has returned a significant amount of capital to shareholders through buybacks since the end of 2021. Over that time, the company's share count has dropped by approximately 18%, with EMCOR repurchasing around $2.4 billion worth of shares.

Watch AI Buybacks in Next Reporting Cycle

Next quarter, it will be worth monitoring the level of buyback spending among these names and other AI stocks. If buyback spending comes in much higher than in the previous quarter, it would suggest that these companies actually took advantage of the midterm election sell-off.

This could inspire confidence, suggesting these firms are not overly worried about the AI buildout slowing. This is particularly true for Lam and EMCOR, given that they are direct plays on AI infrastructure, while Dynatrace is a second-order software beneficiary. Last quarter, buyback spending at these names was approximately $1 billion for Lam, $246 million for Dynatrace, and $190 million for EMCOR.

news.Title: TSM's $2 Billion Packaging Deal Could Ease a Critical AI Bottleneck
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM is adding outside manufacturing support to one of the most constrained parts of its artificial intelligence supply chain. A five-year, $2 billion agreement with GlobalFoundries Inc. GFS will establish another source of silicon interposers for TSM's CoWoS advanced-packaging ecosystem.

That matters because back-end capacity remains constrained even as AI-related demand expands. Packaging availability can limit how quickly wafer demand becomes finished product revenue, making added interposer supply strategically important.

TSM Adds a U.S. Source for CoWoS Interposers

GlobalFoundries plans to manufacture silicon interposers at its Malta, NY, facility, with volume production expected to begin ramping in the first half of 2028. The agreement gives TSM a U.S.-based source for a component used in advanced packages and provides a framework for future capacity expansion.

The arrangement also broadens TSM's manufacturing support beyond its own facilities. GlobalFoundries said the program is designed to expand capacity over time as customer demand grows, giving the partnership room to scale beyond the initial commitment.

TSM Could Gain More Packaging Capacity

CoWoS sits within TSM's broader 3DFabric portfolio, which combines chip stacking and advanced packaging technologies to connect logic, memory and other components. That integration is increasingly important as customers build larger computing systems that require more components to work together efficiently.

Additional interposer supply could eventually help TSM support customers moving toward larger and more complex AI packages. Management said CoWoS remains the leading choice for customers and noted that TSM is already producing packages at five times reticle size while developing larger formats.

TSM Still Faces a Long Ramp to 2028

The deal does not solve the current bottleneck. Qualification work and production execution still need to occur before the planned 2028 volume ramp, leaving near-term back-end constraints in place.

TSM has acknowledged a shortage in back-end supply and said demand remains above its current ability to supply. Until outside capacity arrives, revenue conversion will continue to depend on internal expansion, tool conversions, productivity gains and better capacity utilization.

TSM's AI Supply Chain Gets More Flexible

Outside manufacturing support adds flexibility to TSM's broader capacity strategy. Rather than relying on a single source for every packaging component, the company can combine internal expansion with specialized external supply when that helps customers secure enough front-end and back-end capacity.

That approach fits management's wider planning process, which includes checking data-center construction and electricity availability as well as component supply. Amkor Technology, Inc. AMKR is pursuing a similar industry opportunity by expanding its Arizona advanced-packaging and test campus, with planned investment rising to about $12 billion as customer commitments increase.

Story Continues

TSM's Ratings Support a Selective Bull Case

The GlobalFoundries agreement strengthens the long-term packaging capacity story, but execution remains central. The benefit depends on successful qualification, a timely 2028 ramp and TSM's ability to coordinate wafer output, packaging availability and customer infrastructure readiness.

TSM currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Its Growth Score of B supports the earnings and AI-demand case, while the Value Score of D, Momentum Score of F and VGM Score of D call for greater selectivity. The mix favors investors focused on growth characteristics, but the weaker value and momentum readings temper the near-term setup.

news.Title: Can Applied Materials Capitalize on Rising HBM Demand in 2026?
news.Content:
Applied Materials AMAT is benefiting from the growing demand for AI infrastructure, as it is creating opportunities for the company, especially because semiconductor manufacturers seek to expand DRAM production and address increasing HBM requirements. Higher memory demand could encourage investments in manufacturing capacity, advanced deposition, etch and inspection technologies, driving AMAT's growth.

AMAT is also positioned to benefit from the growing complexity of HBM production and advanced packaging. However, the benefits depend on sustained customer capital spending, as memory remains a cyclical industry. Per management, most leading-edge DRAM fabs are running at full capacity.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, DRAM revenues within Semiconductor Systems rose 52% year over year to a record level. Applied Materials also introduced enhanced Centura Prime epitaxy and Producer Avila 2 PECVD to improve DRAM performance and enable higher-layer-count HBM.

Management expects a sizable increase in DRAM revenues during the second half of 2026, keeping memory-related process spending central to the company's growth profile. Furthermore, as the demand for memory is expanding at a rapid pace and suppliers are essentially unable to match the demand with supply, further investments in fabrication facilities are expected to benefit AMAT.

Applied Materials now expects advanced packaging revenues to grow more than 70% in 2026, up from its prior outlook of more than 50%. The company is extending its portfolio across HBM and 3D chiplet stacking with Nokota VMax 2 plating, Opta Quad CMP and two new eBeam systems for metrology and defect analysis. These factors are likely to remain a tailwind for AMAT in 2026 and beyond.

How Competitors Fare Against AMAT

AMAT's broad portfolio positions the company to capture a larger share of customer spending as semiconductor manufacturing becomes increasingly materials-intensive while also keeping its competitors like Lam Research LRCX and Camtek CAMT at bay. The breadth of Applied Materials' portfolio also reduces its dependence on any single semiconductor technology cycle and supports stronger pricing power.

Camtek focuses on semiconductor inspection, metrology, advanced packaging and high-performance computing applications. Lam Research competes with Applied Materials across deposition and etch technologies, including advanced atomic layer deposition systems used in leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing.

news.Title: Wall Street Analysts Believe Entegris (ENTG) Could Rally 27.44%: Here's is How to Trade
news.Content:
Shares of Entegris (ENTG) have gained 6.3% over the past four weeks to close the last trading session at $147.41, but there could still be a solid upside left in the stock if short-term price targets of Wall Street analysts are any indication. Going by the price targets, the mean estimate of $187.86 indicates a potential upside of 27.4%.

The mean estimate comprises 14 short-term price targets with a standard deviation of $25.3. While the lowest estimate of $135.00 indicates a 8.4% decline from the current price level, the most optimistic analyst expects the stock to surge 52% to reach $224.00. It's very important to note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is a much-coveted metric for investors, solely banking on this metric to make an investment decision may not be wise at all. That's because the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable.

However, an impressive consensus price target is not the only factor that indicates a potential upside in ENTG. This view is strengthened by the agreement among analysts that the company will report better earnings than what they estimated earlier. Though a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't give any idea as to how much the stock could surge, it has proven effective in predicting an upside.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?

They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.

However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

Story Continues

That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

Why ENTG Could Witness a Solid Upside

There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. And that could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. After all, empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 11.1%, as six estimates have moved higher while one has gone lower.

Moreover, ENTG currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), which means it is in the top 5% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much ENTG could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

news.Title: Don't Overlook Cirrus Logic (CRUS) International Revenue Trends While Assessing the Stock
news.Content:
Have you evaluated the performance of Cirrus Logic's (CRUS) international operations during the quarter that concluded in September 2026? Considering the extensive worldwide presence of this chipmaker, analyzing the patterns in international revenues is crucial for understanding its financial resilience and potential for growth.

In the current era of a tightly interconnected global economy, the proficiency of a company to penetrate international markets significantly influences its financial health and trajectory of growth. For investors, the key is to grasp how reliant a company is on overseas markets, as this provides insights into the durability of its earnings, its ability to exploit different economic cycles, and its overall growth capabilities.

Presence in international markets can act as a hedge against domestic economic downturns and provide access to faster-growing economies. However, this diversification also brings complexities due to currency fluctuations, geopolitical risks and differing market dynamics.

Upon examining CRUS' recent quarterly performance, we noticed several interesting patterns in the revenue generated from its international segments, which are commonly analyzed and observed by Wall Street experts.

The company's total revenue for the quarter amounted to $559.46 million, showing decrease of 0.3%. We will now explore the breakdown of CRUS' overseas revenue to assess the impact of its international operations.

A Dive into CRUS' International Revenue Trends

During the quarter, China contributed $329.52 million in revenue, making up 58.9% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $292.05 million, this meant a surprise of +12.83%. Looking back, China contributed $216.71 million, or 47.1%, in the previous quarter, and $302.95 million, or 54%, in the same quarter of the previous year.

Of the total revenue, $17.61 million came from Rest of World during the last fiscal quarter, accounting for 3.2%. This represented a surprise of -92.84% as analysts had expected the region to contribute $245.8 million to the total revenue. In comparison, the region contributed $19.43 million, or 4.2%, and $254.98 million, or 45.5%, to total revenue in the previous and year-ago quarters, respectively.

Revenue Projections for Overseas Markets

The current fiscal quarter's total revenue for Cirrus Logic, as projected by Wall Street analysts, is expected to reach $554.36 million, reflecting a decline of 4.5% from the same quarter last year. The breakdown of this revenue by foreign region is as follows: China is anticipated to contribute 66.3% or $367.3 million, and Rest of World 40.9% or $226.45 million.

Story Continues

For the full year, a total revenue of $1.98 billion is expected for the company, reflecting a decline of 0.7% from the year before. The revenues from China and Rest of World are expected to make up 55.3%, and 47.5% of this total, corresponding to $1.1 billion, and $942.47 million, respectively.

Wrapping Up

Cirrus Logic's reliance on international markets for revenues offers both opportunities and risks. Hence, keeping an eye on its international revenue trends could significantly help forecast the company's prospects.

In an era of growing international ties and escalating geopolitical disputes, financial analysts on Wall Street pay keen attention to these developments to fine-tune their earnings estimations for businesses operating across borders. news.Title: Can Onto Innovation Sustain Its Growth Momentum in 2027?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation ONTO is entering 2027 with strong growth momentum, powered by increasing investments in AI infrastructure, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, HBM production, next-generation logic and memory technologies, and advanced packaging technologies. Revenue reached $410 million in the third quarter, up 19% sequentially and nearly 90% year over year. Power revenue doubled, driven by silicon photonics and power components.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, management projects revenue of $430-$450 million, implying more than 7% sequential growth at the midpoint. That midpoint would bring fiscal 2026 revenue to approximately $1.49 billion, representing growth above 45%. Non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 57.7-58.3%, with a non-GAAP operating margin of 33.5-34.5%. Management expects sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027. Gross margins are expected to exit 2026 above 58%, with quarterly increases of around 50 basis points projected for 2027.

Management expects panel revenue to double in 2026, while existing backlog supports growth exceeding 40% in 2027, with orders extending into 2028. Overall, advanced-packaging revenue is expected to increase more than 80% in 2026. It anticipates further growth exceeding 35% in 2027 as customers increase spending on advanced interconnects and packaging process control.

A key indicator supporting Onto Innovation's 2027 outlook is its rapidly expanding backlog. At the end of the third quarter, its backlog exceeded $1.3 billion, representing growth of 20% during the quarter. Customers are placing orders earlier to secure equipment for multiyear expansion plans, with some commitments extending into 2028, particularly in emerging packaging applications. Management indicated that this backlog reflects customer investment schedules rather than longer equipment delivery lead times. Multi-year customer investment plans could support a more durable revenue trajectory. There is high confidence in the logic and DRAM markets, with more than 35% growth forecasted in 2027.

Intensifying Competition Challenges ONTO's Growth Prospects

KLA Corporation KLAC benefits from AI infrastructure spending, which broadens demand for process control across leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. It raised its calendar 2026 wafer equipment market outlook, including advanced packaging, to the mid-$150 billion range and expects the market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027. KLA anticipates second-half calendar 2026 revenues to grow approximately 25% over the first half, supported by improving supply capacity, expanding backlog and sustained AI-related investments. For the fiscal second quarter, KLA expects revenues of $4.7 billion (+/-$200 million). Non-GAAP earnings are projected at $1.44 per share (+/-11 cents).

Story Continues

Applied Materials AMAT benefits from AI-led investment in leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging, where rising process complexity supports demand for its equipment. It expects a strong 2027, with wafer fab equipment demand projected to grow over 30%, driven by AI-related markets. For the fiscal first quarter, revenue guidance is $11.1 billion, up 58%, with a focus on growth in DRAM, logic and packaging markets. Customers plan to ramp capacity steadily through 2027 and beyond. Applied expects mid-teens growth of about 15% for its MSS segment driven by increased installed base and tool price hikes. AGS operating margins are projected to grow into the high 30s-low 40s%, contributing to long-term margin targets.

news.Title: Bear of the Day: Kimball Electronics (KE)
news.Content:
There's an old saying on Wall Street that the trend is your friend. Unfortunately, sometimes that friend turns out to be the guy who borrows your car, returns it with an empty gas tank, and somehow manages to leave you with a parking ticket. That's the sort of friendship investors have been experiencing with today's Bear of the Day.

The electronics manufacturing industry should be enjoying a pretty favorable environment. Between artificial intelligence, industrial automation, automotive electronics, and increasingly sophisticated medical devices, there is no shortage of demand for advanced electronic components. Yet not every company exposed to these markets is enjoying the same success.

Today's Bear of the Day is Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) Kimball Electronics (KE) . Kimball Electronics is a contract manufacturer specializing in electronic assemblies, circuit boards, and other electronic components used in the automotive, medical, industrial, and public safety markets.

On paper, that's a pretty attractive collection of end markets. The problem is that exposure to attractive industries doesn't automatically translate into attractive earnings. And right now, the earnings estimate revisions are telling a decidedly bearish story.

Kimball Electronics, Inc. Price and Consensus

Kimball Electronics, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Kimball Electronics, Inc. Quote

Analysts Are Heading for the Exits

The primary reason for Kimball Electronics' unfavorable Zacks Rank is the series of negative earnings estimate revisions coming from analysts. Over the last sixty days, one analyst has lowered earnings estimates for the current fiscal year, while none have increased their forecasts. The same pattern holds for next year.

That might not sound particularly dramatic, but remember that Kimball Electronics is a relatively small company with limited analyst coverage. When only three or four analysts are following a stock, even a single downward revision can have a meaningful impact on the consensus.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current fiscal year has declined from approximately $1.58 to $1.50 per share over the last sixty days. Next year's outlook has deteriorated even further. The consensus estimate for the following fiscal year has fallen from $1.82 to approximately $1.71 per share, representing a decline of more than 6%. Here's the problem with those revisions. They're not moving in the direction investors want to see.

Kimball is in the Electronics – Miscellaneous Products industry that ranks in the Top 20% of our Zacks Industry Rank. There are a handful of stocks in this industry that are in the good graces of our Zacks Rank. These include Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks Flex (FLEX) and KLA (KLAC) .

news.Title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Entegris, Ultra Clean and FormFactor
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 16, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Entegris Inc. ENTG, Ultra Clean Holdings Inc. UCTT and FormFactor Inc. FORM.

Here are highlights from Monday's Analyst Blog:

Buy 3 AI Semiconductor Equipment Stocks to Tap Huge Market Opportunity

The global semiconductor manufacturing equipment and materials industry is growing by leaps and bounds, buoyed by artificial intelligence (AI)-driven capital expenditure in leading-edge logic, high-bandwidth memory ("HBM") and Test and Packaging components.

On July 14, SEMI reported in its Mid-Year Total Semiconductor Equipment Forecast – OEM Perspective that the market size of this industry is expected to reach a record high of $165.9 billion globally in 2026, up 23.2% year over year. The momentum is set to continue in the near term, reaching an estimated $229.5 billion globally in 2028.

Here, we recommend three stocks from this space for investment to reap benefits from a potentially vast market. These companies are: Entegris Inc. , Ultra Clean Holdings Inc. and FormFactor Inc.

Each of our picks currently carries either a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Entegris Inc.

Zacks Rank #1 Entegris serves materials, contamination control, equipment and fab construction applications, allowing growth across different phases of semiconductor investment.

AI-related investment supports ENTG's materials and purity products across advanced logic, memory and packaging. Advanced logic represents about 40% of revenues and memory about 30%. In the third quarter of 2026, ENTG secured a 2-nanometer EUV filtration application, an advanced materials plan of record with a major technology provider and multiple CMP wins with memory customers.

ENTG's margin progress reflects strong execution and mix. Adjusted gross margin reached 48.9% in the third quarter of 2026, up from 43.6% a year earlier and 47.6% in the second quarter. Adjusted operating margin increased to 26.8% from 21.1%, while adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 30.2% from 27.3% year-ago. APS adjusted segment margin reached 34.4%.

Strong Guidance

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Entegris expects revenues between $1.025 billion and $1.055 billion, implying about 26% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. GAAP earnings are projected at $1.09-$1.17 per share, while non-GAAP earnings are forecast in the range of $1.32-$1.40.

Story Continues

Management projects an adjusted gross margin of 49.2%-49.7% and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 30.7%-31.2%. Non-GAAP operating expenses are anticipated between $224 million and $230 million. ENTG expects approximately $200 million in capital expenditures for 2026, down from the earlier $250 million plan.

Solid Estimate Revisions

Entegris has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 17% and 58.6%, respectively, for the current year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year's earnings has improved 10.9% over the past 30 days.

ENTG has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 14.3% and 28.1%, respectively, for the next year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for next year's earnings has improved 12.7% over the past 30 days.

Ultra Clean Holdings Inc.

Zacks Rank #2 Ultra Clean reported solid third-quarter 2026 results and its outlook benefits from rising semiconductor equipment demand as AI investment expands across foundry, logic and memory.

UCTT is benefiting from semiconductor capital equipment investment tied to AI infrastructure, with demand broadening across foundry, logic and memory. Leading-edge foundries are expanding capacity for advanced nodes, while memory manufacturers are investing in DRAM, high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

Ultra Clean's UCT 3.0 strategy aims to capture this growth through additional manufacturing capacity and higher-value engineered solutions. UCTT's outsourced model, capacity growth and closer customer design work support share gains. Higher utilization and a richer mix of engineered subsystems offer room for margin expansion. Services should add higher-margin revenue as new fabs increase wafer starts.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Ultra Clean expects revenues between $800 million and $860 million. The midpoint implies sequential revenue growth of approximately 9.4%. UCTT projects non-GAAP earnings per share between $1.11 and $1.35, based on around 48.9 million diluted shares. GAAP earnings per share are expected between $1.02 and $1.26.

Ultra Clean has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 34.8% and more than 100%, respectively, for the current year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year's earnings has improved 11.8% over the past 30 days.

UCTT has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 36.8% and 95%, respectively, for the next year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for next year's earnings has improved 0.6% over the past 30 days.

FormFactor Inc.

Zacks Rank #1 FormFactor is benefiting from robust growth in HBM driven by the rapid adoption of generative AI and high-performance computing. FORM's advanced packaging continues to raise test complexity in DRAM, particularly as HBM evolves toward faster interfaces. Third-quarter 2026 DRAM revenues held near the second-quarter record at $84.9 million despite a shift from HBM to DDR5.

FormFactor's SmartMatrix technology supports testing of completed HBM4 stacks at speeds above 10 gigabits per second. Management expects HBM growth to continue through 2027, citing its HBM4E and HBM5 design pipeline and differentiated final-stack test capability.

FORM's co-packaged optics (CPO) is moving toward production and expanding the Systems opportunity. Systems revenue reached a record $59.5 million in third-quarter 2026, up 23% sequentially, on higher TRITON photonics system demand. Management raised its 2026 TRITON revenue expectation to upwards of $30 million from the initial $10 million to $20 million range.

FORM also serves near-package optics and pluggable applications through wafer-level photonic integrated circuit testing. Its integrated Keystone optical probing technology broadens exposure as customers adopt different photonics architectures.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, FormFactor expects revenues of $285 million, plus or minus $10 million, reflecting continued broad-based demand. Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 54%, plus or minus 150 basis points. Non-GAAP earnings are expected to be 95 cents per share, plus or minus 9 cents.

At the midpoint of its fourth-quarter outlook, FORM expects 2026 revenues to exceed $1 billion for the first time. The company continues to target a longer-term operating model of $1.6 billion in revenues, 55% gross margin and $5 in non-GAAP earnings per share.

FormFactor has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 33% and more than 100%, respectively, for the current year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year's earnings has improved 9.2% over the past 30 days.

FORM has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 21.7% and 29.9%, respectively, for the next year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for next year's earnings has improved 15.9% over the past 30 days.

news.Title: Zacks.com featured highlights include Ralph Lauren, Expedia, NVIDIA and Lam Research
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 16, 2026 – Stocks in this week's article are Ralph Lauren RL, Expedia Group EXPE, NVIDIA NVDA and Lam Research LRCX

4 GARP Stocks That Investors Can Scoop Up for Maximum Returns

If you are looking for a profitable portfolio of stocks offering the best of value and growth investing, you can try the growth at a reasonable price or GARP strategy.

The strategy helps investors gain exposure to undervalued stocks with impressive prospects. Unlike a blend strategy, a portfolio that uses GARP investing is expected to include stocks that offer the best of value and growth investing. Ralph Lauren , Expedia Group , NVIDIA and Lam Research are some GARP stocks that hold promise.

GARP Metrics: Mix of Growth & Value Metrics

The GARP strategy seeks to offer an ideal investment by utilizing the best features of value and growth investing. Investors adopting the GARP approach prefer buying stocks priced below the market or any reasonable target determined by fundamental analysis. These stocks also have solid prospects in terms of cash flow, revenues, earnings per share (EPS) and so on.

Growth Metrics

A strong earnings growth history and impressive earnings prospects are the main concepts that GARP investors borrow from the growth investing strategy. However, instead of super-normal growth rates, pursuing stocks with a more stable and reasonable growth rate is a tactic of GARP investors. Hence, growth rates between 10% and 20% are considered ideal under the GARP strategy.

Another metric that growth and GARP investors consider is return on equity (ROE). GARP investors look for a strong and higher ROE than the industry average to identify superior stocks. Stocks with positive cash flows take precedence under the GARP plan.

Value Metrics

GARP investing prioritizes popular value metrics, the price-to-earnings (P/E) and price-to-book (P/B) ratios. Though this investing style picks stocks with higher P/E ratios than value investors, it avoids companies with extremely high P/E ratios.

Using the GARP principle, we ran a screen to identify stocks that should offer solid returns in the near term.

Here are four stocks from the 15 that made it through the screening process.

Expedia Group entered the holiday quarter with raised full-year guidance, a key near-term stock catalyst. The company now projects 2026 gross bookings of $131.4-$131.9 billion, revenues of $16.37-$16.43 billion and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 1.8-2 points. The fourth-quarter guidance calls for revenues of $3.69-$3.75 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $830-$880 million. Product momentum supports demand.

Story Continues

The Fall 2026 release added more than 30 new and enhanced features, including AI Compare, Activity Planner and Vrbo's AI Voice Agent. In B2B, the Rapid Activities API, enhanced by Tiqets inventory, entered beta, with general availability planned for early 2027. Tiqets activities also reached select UK travel agencies through Expedia TAAP in beta. A $0.48 quarterly dividend, to be paid out on Dec. 10, supports ongoing shareholder returns.

The consensus estimate for EXPE's 2026 earnings has moved north by 0.9% to $20.84 per share in the past 60 days. This Zacks Rank #1 company surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters, with the average surprise being 15.26%.

Ralph Lauren entered the holiday season with raised fiscal 2027 guidance, constant-currency revenue growth centered around 6% to 7% on a 52-week basis, and operating margin expansion of 80 to 100 basis points. Third-quarter growth is guided to be 3% to 4%, including about one point of drag from wholesale timing and off-price reductions.

Its Asia initiatives include the Japan app launch and Polofest in Tokyo, the first activation ahead of the brand's 60th anniversary in 2027. Inventory is down 9% year over year, and $500 million of repurchases completed fiscal 2027 buyback plans, alongside a $1 quarterly dividend. Tariff uncertainty and softer European comparable sales remain risks, while leadership realignments effective Nov. 29 aim to sharpen execution across operations, product and AI.

The consensus estimate for RL's fiscal 2027 earnings per share has moved south by 0.3% to $18.72 in the past 60 days. This Zacks Rank #2 company surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 8.44%.

NVIDIA 's near-term setup rests on guidance and product ramps. Management projects third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, with gross margin near 74.0%, while assuming no China Data Center compute revenues. Vera Rubin, in full production, is running at cloud partners including CoreWeave, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.

In October, NVIDIA's MGX 1.2 rack specification added support for deployments up to 250kW, and Meta is adopting Spectrum-6 Ethernet switches. In September, NVIDIA launched an open agent-safety platform, and the board added $150 billion to the buyback authorization, leaving $235 billion. Leadership is the swing factor. Jensen Huang's Nov. 12 resignation makes CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, though the board expects roadmap continuity.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NVDA's fiscal 2027 earnings per share has moved south by 3.4% to $9.28 in the past 60 days. This Zacks Rank #2 company surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in all four trailing quarters, the average surprise being 5.82%.

Lam Research 's near-term setup rests on guidance and capacity readiness. Its December-quarter guidance calls for revenues of $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million, with non-GAAP gross margin of 52.5% and EPS of $2.33, plus or minus 15 cents. Management links demand to AI-driven device complexity. The Oct. 27 imec collaboration targets 3D integration and Aether dry resist for high-NA EUV patterning, broadening technology relevance.

The company also expects to outgrow wafer fabrication equipment spending. A new 470,000-square-foot Livermore logistics hub, retrieving parts in under 30 seconds, should help the company respond to demand shifts. Capital return, which includes a $25 billion repurchase authorization and a $0.33 quarterly dividend, to be paid out on Jan. 6, 2027, adds support. Execution against guidance, however, remains the key variable.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for LRCX's fiscal 2027 earnings has moved north by 3% to $9.60 per share in the past 60 days. This Zacks Rank #2 company surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in all four trailing quarters, the average surprise being 6.43%.

For the rest of this Screen of the Week article please visit Zacks.com at: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3029625/4-garp-stocks-that-investors-can-scoop-up-for-maximum-returns

news.Title: 群聯第3季EPS狂飆138元  記憶體獲利驚人  上下游兩樣情
news.Content:
台灣記憶體族群第3季財報出爐，受惠AI搶產能推升報價，上下游獲利呈現兩樣情。南亞科、華邦電與旺宏第3季毛利率及獲利同步改寫歷史新高，控制晶片廠群聯單季每股純益更衝上138元；反觀部分模組廠受消費電子需求趨緩與原料墊高夾擊，第3季獲利回檔，供應鏈進入洗牌角力期。

AI應用排擠標準型DRAM產能，帶動上游廠獲利大爆發。南亞科第3季毛利率衝上85.7％，單季每股純益25.4元、前3季49.28元；華邦電與旺宏同步登頂，第3季毛利率各為70.57％與70.49％，前3季每股純益15.32元及10.34元。群聯前3季每股純益狂賺325.49元，模組大廠威剛第3季每股純益38.69元，前3季大賺逾10個股本、每股純益101.47元。

然而手機與個人電腦買氣轉弱、低價庫存效益消退，創見第3季毛利率從77.03％降至56.5％，每股純益滑落至16.11元；宇瞻毛利率從51.25％降至40.08％，每股純益15.34元。研調機構分析，AI伺服器持續吸納原廠產能使DRAM供給吃緊，但終端買氣疲軟限制模組廠轉嫁空間，導致漲價紅利集中在上游。

宇瞻預期明年上半年DRAM缺貨將加劇，已採惜售策略預留貨源卡位，雖須提列損失影響第3季獲利；NAND Flash因新增應用有限、供需平緩，模組廠毛利率將隨庫存去化回歸常態，明年各廠獲利關鍵將取決於DRAM貨源掌握度。
